REPORT
The Report of the Committee deals with the Action Taken by the Government on the
recommendations contained in its One Hundred Eighty Fifth Report on Demands for Grants of the
Ministry of Home Affairs for the years (2015-16).   The said Report was presented to the Rajya
Sabha on 23
rd April, 2015 and laid on the Table of the Lok Sabha on 24 th April, 2015.
2. Action Taken Note was received from the Ministry of Home Affairs in respect of the
recommendations contained in the Report on 27 th August 2015. The Minister of Home Affairs has
not yet laid on the Table of the Lok Sabha and the Rajya Sabha the statement on the status of
implementation of recommendations contained in that Report. The Action Taken Note received from
the Ministry of Home Affairs has been categorized as follows:
Chapter-I:  The recommendations/Observations, which have been accepted by the Government:
Para Nos. 3.3.18, 3.3.19, 4.3.6, 4.3.7, 4.4.32 (of One Hundred and Eighty Fifth Report)
T
OTAL Recommendations-5
The Committee is pleased to note that the Ministry has accepted its recommendations as
mentioned in Chapter-I of the Report.
Chapter-II:  The recommendations/observations which the Committee does not desire to pursue in
view of the Government’s replies: Para Nos. 2.17, 2.18, 2.19, 3.1.9, 3.1.12, 3.3.7, 3.3.25, 3.3.27,
4.2.11, 4.4.9, 4.4.19, 4.4.24, 4.4.29, 5.1.12, 5.1.13, 5.2.3, 5.3.2, 5.4.8, 5.4.9, 5.5.2, 5.6.4 (ibid)
T
OTAL Recommendations-21
The Committee is convinced with the explanations furnished by the Ministry and, therefore,
does not want to pursue the recommendations further.
Chapter-III:  The recommendations/observations in respect of which the Committee is not satisfied
with the replies of the Ministry: Para Nos. 2.10, 2.12, 3.1.5, 3.3.17, 3.3.31, 4.1.17, 4.2.12, 4.3.5,
4.3.8, 4.4.16, 4.4.22 (ibid) T
OTAL Recommendations-11
The Committee expresses its concern over the non-implementation of its recommendations
contained in Chapter - III and desires that the Ministry should furnish convincing explanations in
respect of those recommendations.
Chapter-IV:  Recommendations/Observations in respect of which final replies of the Government
have not been received: Para Nos. 2.9, 2.25, 4.1.10, 3.3.32, 4.2.10, 4.2.13, 4.4.33, 5.1.14, 5.2.6,
5.2.7, 5.2.8, 5.4.10 (ibid) T
OTAL Recommendations-12
In respect of 12 recommendations in Chapter-IV , the Ministry has either furnished interim
reply or couched its response in vague terms. Therefore, the Committee desires that the Ministry
should furnish pointed and detailed Action Taken Notes in respect of the recommendations
categorized in Chapter - IV in keeping with the spirit of the recommendations.
3. The details of the ATRs have been analysed in various Chapters in the succeeding chapters.

CHAPTER-I
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERV ATIONS WHICH HA VE BEEN ACCEPTED BY THE
GOVERNMENT
1.1 DEMAND NO. 56
Recommendation
1.1.1 The Committee strongly recommends that the Government must give emphasis on return of
migrants to the valley. (Para 3.3.18)
Action Taken
1.1.2 The Government is committed to facilitate the return of the Kashmiri migrants to the
Kashmir V alley and their proper rehabilitation there. The Government has earmarked `320 crore for
the rehabilitation of the Kashmiri Migrants in the Union Budget of 2015-16.
1.1.3 An integrated proposal for the return and rehabilitation of the Kashmiri migrants is also
being prepared in consultation with the stakeholders.
Further Recommendation
1.1.4 The committee while acknowledging the efforts of the Government of India
recommends that the initiatives of the Government should reflect on the ground.
Recommendation
1.1.5 The Committee took note of the fact that under Plan Scheme “Special Industry Initiative
for J&K”, the Ministry had projected 
` 130.00 crore in 2014-15, however, it was allocated ` 90.00
crore in BE 2014-15 which was further reduced to ` 52.45 crore at RE stage.  The Committee
observes with dismay that in spite of the 100% utilization of funds under this scheme, the Finance
Ministry has allocated a meager amount of ` 45.00 crore for this scheme against projected demand
of ` 120.00 crore for 2015-16.  The Committee recommends that the Finance Ministry should look
positively into  the projected demand of ` 120 crore of the Ministry while sanctioning additional
amount at RE stage as this scheme is targeted to bring back Kashmiri youths into mainstream so
that they do not fall prey to anti national activities. (Para 3.3.19)
Action Taken
1.1.6 Depending upon the pace of expenditure, proposal for additional amount will be submitted
to Ministry of Finance, at the RE stage.
1.2 DEPRESSION IN CAPFs
Recommendation
1.2.1 The Committee is sympathetic to the desperate situation of paramilitary forces personnel.
2

3
The Committee feels that the Government should look into their agonies through which they pass
while working in difficult circumstances.  The Committee understands that when the personnel of
paramilitary forces pass thorough stress and feel de-motivated and demoralized it would have far
reaching negative repercussions.  The Committee, therefore, recommends that the Government should
look into the long pending grievances of the paramilitary personnel and address them in a time
bound manner. (Para 4.3.6)
Action Taken
1.2.2 On receipt of the grievance from the serving/retired personnel or from their spouse or from
NOKs of the deceased personnel regarding maintenance of family, non receipt of pension/family
pension, and other terminal dues etc., the same is forwarded to all concerned offices i.e. Sector,
Range, Group Centre and unit with the instructions to settle their grievances within prescribed time
frame. The applicant is also apprised with the factual position/ status with reference to his/her
grievance within the stipulated time.
1.2.3 Further, the Force Headquarters also take care of the personal grievances of the officials
regarding their promotions/transfers and other related service matters through personal audiences,
representations/ petitions etc.
Recommendation
1.2.4 The Committee understands that years of working in hostile conditions by CAPFs personnel
and staying away from their family, long working hours, sleep deprivation, denial of leave, etc.
take a toll on their lives.  The Committee recommends that the paramilitary forces should introduce
Yoga and other stress management techniques in the CAPFs to de-stress these personnel. The
Committee also recommends that the personnel long posted in difficult areas should be transferred
to relatively normal area after a fixed duration. Special allowances aspect should also be examined.
(Para 4.3.7)
Action Taken
1.2.5 Sufficient periods of Yoga and Stress Management have been included in the Training
Syllabus in order to promote the Yoga and to de-stress the CAPFs personnel working in
uncongenial condition and far flung areas.
1.2.6 As regards posting of the personnel from difficult areas to relatively normal areas after a
fixed duration, it is submitted that each CAPF has a transfer policy for rotational transfer of its
personnel between hard and soft/static locations. The transfer policy is followed uniformly in the
Force. Choice postings given by the Force personnel are considered by the Force to post them at
the desired place of posting as far as practicable and administratively possible.
Further Recommendation
1.2.7 The Committee is of opinion that these techniques should not only become part of
training syllabus but also be added in their everyday routine. Regarding transfer posting in
these forces, the Committee hopes that mechanism to decide over  choice postings remains
transparent and free from nepotism etc.

4
1.3 SENSITISATION TOWARDS ETHICAL AND MORAL VALUES
Recommendation
1.3.1 The Committee notes the submissions made by the Home Secretary and Delhi Police
Commissioner for making Delhi Police a true reflection of cosmopolitan composition of Delhi
Police.  The Committee recommends that the recruitment to the posts of constabulary should also
be done by Staff Selection Commission (SSC) as has been done in the case of post of Sub-
Inspectors. The recruitment on the basis of All India test conducted by SSC in itself is a practical
solution in this regard where people from the whole country can apply. The Committee hopes that
Delhi Police would soon have all India character and be more representative and broad based.
(Para 4.4.32)
Action Taken
1.3.2 In order to give the Delhi Police a true cosmopolitan character, the Delhi Police is going
to get online exam of Delhi Police Constable (Executive) on All India basis through Staff Selection
Commission as is being done in case of Sub-Inspector (Exe.). Recently the Senior Officers of
Delhi Police had attended a meeting in DOPT on 11.05.2015 for online exam through SSC. In the
meeting it was decided to prepare MOU in this regard.  Further steps are being taken by Delhi
Police on priority basis.

CHAPTER-II
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERV ATIONS ON WHICH
THE COMMITTEE DOES NOT DESIRE TO PURSUE THE MATTER
IN VIEW OF THE GOVERNMENT’S REPLY
2.1 OVERALL ASSESSMENT OF DEMANDS FOR GRANTS
Recommendation
2.1.1 The Committee notes the courses of actions undertaken by the Government in terms of
maintaining internal security scenario in the country. The Committee also notes the submission that
multi pronged strategies being followed in the short and medium term have led to a declining trend
in the level of Left Wing violence as well as the resultant killings since 2011. The Committee,
however, desires that the Ministry of Home Affairs as per its topmost priority should strive
diligently to improve the capacity infrastructure of Central Para Military Forces and upgrade the
much necessary institutional mechanisms for further enhancing internal security of the country.
(Para 2.17)
Action Taken
2.1.2 The Central Government has adopted an integrated approach to deal with the problem of
Left Wing Extremism (LWE) simultaneously pursuing the issues relating to security, development,
enforcement of rights and entitlements of local communities and public perception management.
The State Governments spearhead all efforts to control the LWE activities in the States. The Central
Government closely monitors the situation and supplements the efforts of the State Governments
over a wide range of security and development related interventions. The underlying philosophy is
to enhance the capacity of the State Governments to tackle the menace of LWE in a concerted
manner.
2.1.3 Apart from providing Central Armed Police Force (CAPF) battalions to assist the State
Police Forces in counter-LWE operations, the Government of India has been providing assistance
for capacity building of the States through the Security Related Expenditure (SRE) Scheme, the
Special Infrastructure Scheme and the Scheme for Construction/ Strengthening of Fortified Police
Stations.
2.1.4 At present, a total of 110 battalions of CAPFs are provided to the States of Andhra Pradesh,
Bihar, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, Odisha, Telangana, Uttar Pradesh
and West Bengal in counter-LWE operations.
2.1.5 It is the belief of Government of India that through a combination of security and
development related interventions, the LWE problem can be successfully contained. It is worth
mentioning that due to the measures adopted by the Government, LWE violence has significantly
declined in the last four years i.e. 2011 to 2014.
5

6
Institutional Mechanism: -
2.1.6 State Governments are primarily responsible for Law and Order, countering internal
disturbances, terrorists and naxalite activities. The CAPFs are made available to the State
Governments on the latter’s request to assist them in maintenance of public order.  As per SOP ,
during deployment, infrastructure and other logistics are provided by the State
Government However, before any deployment of CAPFs on long term basis, a joint meeting of all
the stake holders is organized to firm up the infrastructural plan and deployment plan of CAPFs.
CAPFs are deployed once the requisite infrastructure outlined in the SOP is put in place by the
State Government concerned. Further, there is a mechanism of quarterly meeting of Joint Audit of
CAPFs and the State Governments about the review of the operations as well as infrastructure. The
report of the joint audit are further reviewed in MHA and corrective measures are undertaken to
further strengthen the infrastructure required. The periodical review is aimed at ensuring the
optimum utilization of the CAPFs in the overall interest of the internal security of the country. 
2.1.7 To improve the basic infrastructure of CAPFs and upgrade essential institutional
mechanisms for further enhancing internal security of the country, during 12
th Five Year Plan,
(financial years 2012-13, 2013-14 and 2014-15), 15306 nos. of dwelling units and 278 nos. of
Barracks were targeted for construction. Out of this 9379 nos. of dwelling units and 245 nos. of
Barracks have been constructed till 31.03.2015. For remaining financial year 2015-16 and 2016-17,
8900 nos. of dwelling units and 160 nos. of Barracks have been targeted for construction.
Recommendation
2.1.8 The Committee notes the national policy and action plan document which adopted an
integrated strategy comprising security related measures, development related measures, ensuring
rights and entitlements related measures and public perception management to contain Left Wing
Extremism in the country.  The Committee understands that only security related measures cannot
check growth of Left Wing Extremism. It should go along with development measures and
strategies. (Para 2.18)
Action Taken
2.1.9 The National Policy and Action Plan to address LWE problem has been documented with
the approval of the Union Home Minister and has been sent to States and other stakeholders for
its implementation. The policy document has adopted an integrated four pronged strategy
comprising Security related measures, Development related measures, ensuring Rights and
Entitlements related measures and Public Perception Management.
2.1.10 Development remains a key prong of National strategy and Ministries of the Central
Government as well as the State Governments are working in synergy towards this end. Some
important development initiatives currently under implementation are:-
(a) Road Requirement Plan;
(b) Improvement of Rail Connectivity;
(c) Installation of Mobile Towers project;
(d) Improvement of education and health infrastructure;

7
(e) Minimum Support Price (MSP) for minor forest produce;
(f) Support for Adivasi festivals/ cultural programmes; and
(g) Increased reach of All India Radio (AIR/FM) and Doordarshan in LWE affected
areas.
Recommendation
2.1.11 The Committee is of the opinion that the development of socio-economic infrastructure and
services such as schools, Primary Health Centres, roads, bridges, etc. should go hand in hand with
security operations in Left Wing Extremism Affected areas. The Committee is of the considered view
that providing basic infrastructure and other facilities can help check growth of influence of left
wing extremism in these areas. (Para 2.19)
Action Taken
2.1.12 The Central Government has adopted an integrated approach to deal with the menace of
Left Wing Extremism (LWE) in the areas of security, development, enforcing rights and
entitlements of local communities and public perception management. The State Governments
specifically deal with various issues related to LWE activities in the States. The Central Government
closely monitors the situation and supplements the efforts of the State Governments over a wide
range of measures both on security and development fronts.
2.1.13 On the development front, the Central Government is implementing special schemes like the
Road Requirement Plan for improvement of roads, projects for installation of mobile towers,
improvement of rail connectivity, education and health infrastructure in the LWE affected areas.
2.1.14 The scheme titled ‘Additional Central Assistance (ACA) for LWE affected districts’ is also
under implementation for accelerated development of the affected areas. The aim of this initiative
is to provide public infrastructure and services such as School Buildings, Anganwadi Centres,
Primary Health Centres (PHCs), Drinking Water Supply, Village Roads, Electric Lights in public
places such as PHCs and schools etc. in the affected/contiguous districts. As on 19.5.2015, a total
amount of ` 9,059.00 crore of central fund has been released under the ACA to the 88 districts
covered under the Scheme and against which an expenditure of ` 8,450.85 crore (93.29 %) has
been reported. The number of Projects completed so far under the ACA is 1,32,708. However, as
a policy decision starting from the year 2015-16, it has been left to the States to continue with
this scheme out of their increased resources in consequence of the recommendation of the 14
th
Finance Commission.
2.2 DEMAND NO. 53 - MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS
Recommendation
2.2.1 The Committee in this connection also notes that the proposal for issuance of National
Identity Card to the Citizens of India, who are of age 18 years and above, is under consideration.
The Committee feels proposal of  having National Identity Card to the Citizens of India  needs
to be examined  keeping in mind  presence of successful Voter I Card scheme, which is given to

8
the citizens of India of 18 years age and above. The Committee also understands that linking of
Aadhar numbers with the voter I-cards is underway and therefore voter I cards will also have
biometric details. In view of the Committee, this arrangement seems sufficient. The Committee
therefore desires that all possible steps should be taken to avoid the duplication of efforts between
different agencies of the Government as well as avoidable expenditure from public exchequer.
(Para 3.1.9)
Action Taken
2.2.2 The Citizenship Act 1955 was amended in 2004 by inserting Section 14A which inter-alia
provides for the following:
z The Central Government may compulsorily register every citizen of India and issue
National Identity Card to them.
z The Central Government may maintain a National Register of Indian Citizens (NRIC)
and for that purpose establish a National Registration Authority (NRA).
2.2.3 Accordingly, the creation of National Population Register (NPR), the first building block
towards carving out NRIC, has been undertaken as per the provisions of the Citizenship Act, 1955.
The demographic data for NPR has already been collected for the entire country in 2010 and got
digitized, thereby creating an electronic database of approx. 119 crore persons. Biometric enrolment
has been completed for more than 28.42 crore persons.
2.2.4 To minimize the duplication of efforts, in terms of the capture of biometrics, a synergy was
developed between NPR & UIDAI. 12 States/ UTs were given to NPR and 24 States/ UTs to
UIDAI for biometric enrolment. Further, if a person indicates she/ he is already enrolled for
aadhaar, the biometric data was not captured for NPR instead the aadhaar number was recorded
to source the biometric data from UIDAI.
2.2.5 W ith regard to other databases already in place, viz., Ration Card, Passport, Driving License
etc. in general and Election Commission of India’s Electoral Rolls in particular, which are provided
to Citizens of India,  these are based on self verification and not on physical verification at the
ground level.  Accordingly, after due deliberations within the Government, a decision was taken by
the Government to let the NPR complete its mandate by scrupulously following the laid down
approved procedures in the statute book.
2.2.6 The proposal to carve out NRIC from NPR is under consideration of the Government.
This would further address national security concerns and facilitate more effective execution of
social programmes and ensure a robust delivery mechanism.
Recommendation
2.2.7 The Committee recommends that the allocation under NCRMP should be enhanced at RE
stage as to address cyclone risks and mitigation in two States – Odisha and Andhra Pradesh during

was projected by  the Ministry which already have liability of over ` 100 crores of the previous

Action Taken

2.2.9 However, the additional demand for funds will be made at RE stage if required for NCRMP
Phase-I & II.

Recommendation
2.7.1 The Committee empathizes with general perception about police in the country. The
Committee is of the opinion that a person in distress only comes to police station or contacts police
personnel for help.  In such a situation if police personnel at the police station do not behave like
a protector of law & order, it causes further problem to the person in distress. The Committee
recommends that a training programme of long duration on ethical and moral values and people
friendly attitude should be imparted to police personnel especially of lower ranks.  The Committee
is of the opinion that the Government should not only emphasise on the security training of police
personnel but also train them for developing good communication skills, behavior, attitude and
responsibility with the general public.  The Committee is of the considered view that Government
of India should issue guidelines to all the States and Union Territories in this regard.
(Para 4.4.24)
Action Taken
DELHI POLICE

trainees are imbibed with ethical and moral values throughout their training period.  Emphasis is
laid particularly on citizen friendly behavior and communication skills.  In the present scenario, it
is imperative that attitude and behavior of the police staff especially the lower rung which is usually
the first responders, should be extremely courteous.  To achieve these goals, police training, both
at induction level and specialized training during service is focused on this aspect.  Eminent faculty
from diverse fields are regularly invited to interact with trainees to share their valuable experiences
and professionals are also called to teach soft skills and basic usage of spoken English.
2.7.3 The specialized courses are conducted for in service personnel to inculcate in them people
friendly attitude and right behavior with public:-
(i) Sensitization of staff functioning with women help Desk/DO/DD Writer/Receptionist at
Police Station.
(ii) Course on Soft Skills.
(iii) Course on Human Rights.
(iv) Course on Gender Sensitization.
(v) Course on stress and time management.
(vi) Course on Empathy.
(vii) Course for police personnel towards issues concerning visually impaired and
differently abled persons.
(viii) Course on issues pertaining to persons belonging to NE states, backward sections of
society, women & children.

13
2.7.4 Moreover, Delhi Police is constantly improvising course material keeping in view the

(2) 20% of vacancies in the Border Guarding Forces (BGFs) (BSF, ITBP, SSB & Assam
Rifles) are allotted to border districts, which fall within the responsibility of the Force.
(3) 20% of vacancies in BGFs are allotted to areas affected by militancy i.e. J&K, North
Eastern States and naxal affected areas. The districts/ areas affected by militancy are
notified by the Government from time to time.
(4) In Forces, other than BGFs, 40% vacancies are allotted to militancy affected areas i.e.
J&K, North Eastern States and naxal affected areas. The district/areas affected by
militancy are notified by the Government from time to time.
2.13.4 Thus, in each Force candidates are selected from each State/UT as per the prescribed
quota. However, a CAPF does not have sufficient number of locations/ offices in each State/Region
of the Country on uniform basis. Presence of a Force depend upon its area of responsibility
(AOR). For example the ITBP , SSB, BSF and AR (Border Guarding Forces) has relatively low
presence in South and South-west part of the Country. Therefore, it is practically not possible to
always post the Force person in or near his Home State. However, all the CAPFs make the best
effort to give posting in or near the Home State on rotation basis post as far as possible.

Recommendation
3.1.1 In principle, the Committee is in favour of the financial autonomy of the States as
recommended by the 14
th Finance Commission. However, the Committee is of the considered view
that the matter of national pursuits ranging from national security to territorial integrity cannot
be left at the dispensation of the State Governments alone with no monitoring and accountability
of Union Government in spite of clear constitutional mandate to the Union Government to the
effect. As also highlighted by the Home Secretary that the issue of transferring the national security
related Scheme to the States should be reviewed and the Central Government must have a say in
the matter of national importance, particularly pertaining to internal security. The Committee is of
the considered view that the Government must be cautious while transferring such schemes/ projects/
plans having grave national ramifications, to the States so that national security is not
compromised in the name of the financial autonomy to the States. Moreover, the Committee strongly
recommends that even if any centrally Sponsored Scheme is transferred to the States, the Central
Government must have resilient monitoring mechanism over the progress of implementation of those
schemes. The Committee recommends that the Finance Ministry should positively look into the
matter and reconsider its decision of transferring eight Centrally Sponsored Schemes of MHA
merged into an Umbrella Centrally Sponsored Scheme called ‘National Scheme for Modernization
of Police and other Forces’. (Para 2.10)

3.7.7 As and when information is received in the Vigilance Unit regarding inaction in registering
FIR, an Action Taken Report is immediately taken from the District concerned. The Vigilance Unit
is an independent Unit which monitors complaints against police personnel. This is in addition to
the option available to the complainant to directly approach local police authorities at senior level
and have necessary action taken on their complaint.
3.7.8 At present, Delhi Police has an inbuilt mechanism to address complaints of non-registration
of FIR.  Apart from the Vigilance Unit of Delhi Police, all supervisory officers of the Districts and
Ranges promptly look into any complaint of non-registration of cases. Complaints of non-
registration are also scrutinized in the Police Headquarters and the defaulting staff are identified for
suitable corrective action.  Calling of explanation is mandatory as the officer needs to be given an
opportunity to explain the reasons for not registering the FIR. If the reasons are not found
convincing, based on the seriousness of the situation, further necessary departmental action is
taken.
3.7.9 As for constitution of independent body to look into such complaints, at present Delhi
Police is accountable to several Commissions such as National Human Rights Commission, Public
Grievances Commission, Central Vigilance Commission, etc. and complaints of non-registration are
also monitored by the Courts of Law.
Further Recommendation
3.7.10 The committee is dismayed to note that out of 50 complaints for not lodging of FIRs,
only 2 complaints were found to be genuine. The committee is not convinced with the
information provided and  surprised to find that complainants made complains for non-
registration of their FIRs and it was found by vigilance unit that FIRs were already lodged
in respective police stations which indicates that even though a FIR was lodged the
complainant made complaint that FIR was not lodged which apparently seems unacceptable.
The Committee would like to be apprised of time and date of such complaints and FIRs
lodged in such cases. The committee reiterates its earlier recommendation that there should
be non-official Members of vigilance unit drawn from other government agencies, human
rights organizations, civil society organizations etc. to look into such complaint. It is then
only, impartiality and proper check and balance can be ensured and conflict of interest can
be avoided.

4.5 SENSITISATION TOWARDS ETHICAL AND MORAL VALUES
Recommendation
4.5.1 The Committee raised the issue of duty hours of Delhi police personnel and allowances paid
for extra working hours. The Commissioner of Police, Delhi replied that officially there is fixed
duty hour, however, it is not possible to follow. He added that there is no provision of
compensatory leave and extra working hours allowances to Delhi Police personnel. The Committee
understands that in view of the nature of work, it is not practically possible to follow fixed duty
hours in Delhi Police. However, the Committee feels that the police personnel working extra hours
should be given allowance/compensation, etc. to keep them motivated. Subject to the exigency of
work, there should also be provision for compensatory leave for personnel deployed during
holidays. (Para 4.4.33)
Action Taken
4.5.2 In 1979, the Government of India sanctioned one month’s extra pay as compensatory pay
to the non-gazetted police personnel of Delhi Police in lieu of performing long hours of duty and
their inability to avail themselves of the holidays and weekly off days as they are not only required
to be on duty on most of the public holidays like Republic Day, Independence Day, Dussehra,
Diwali and Moharram etc. but also have to put in extra hours of work so as to maintain public
peace and order. Further, the police personnel, on a number of occasions, are not able to avail
holidays even on Sundays. Restrictions are also imposed on grant of casual leave/earned leave
depending upon the prevailing law and order.  Thus, the number of days of extra work put in by
Delhi Police personnel is much more than the compensatory pay of 30 days payable to the rank
of Constable to Inspector.

35
4.5.3 Besides this, the pay scales of police personnel in the UT of Chandigarh and in the State
of Punjab are higher than what are being paid in Delhi. Pay scales of police personnel in U.P . are
more or equivalent to that of Delhi Police. All these three UT/States are giving one month’s pay
as compensatory pay to their police personnel in addition to other benefits which are not available
to Delhi Police.
4.5.4 Commitments of Delhi Police have also increased manifold. The terrorists activities and
threats to VVIPs and other persons, to be provided with security of Delhi Police under various
categories, have been increasing day by day. Similarly, the number of agitations, demonstrations/
processions and other law & order situations have been on the increase all through and more so
during recent times.
4.5.5 In view of above, a proposal to enhance the compensatory pay upto 60 days in a calendar
year for all the ranks of Delhi Police has been submitted by Delhi Police to 7
th Central Pay
Commission for their recommendation.

Scheme have been transferred to the State Governments. Out of these components, Modernization
of State Police Forces, Crime and Criminal Tracking Network and Systems (CCTNS) to ensure

REPORT
The Report of the Committee deals with the Action Taken by the Government on the
recommendations contained in its One Hundred Eighty Third Report on the Problems being Faced
by Refugees and Displaced Persons in J&K. The said Report was presented to the Rajya Sabha
on 22nd December, 2014 and laid on the Table of the Lok Sabha on 22nd December, 2014.
2. Action Taken Notes were received from the Ministry of Home Affairs in respect of the
recommendations contained in the Report on 24th June, 2015 whereupon Rajya Sabha Secretariat
vide its communication dated 5th November, 2015 forwarded a detailed questionnaire to the
Ministry of Home Affairs which in turn furnished the replies thereof on 4th December, 2015.  The
Committee considered the Action Taken Notes and the said replies of the Ministry and the same
have been categorized as under:
Chapter-I: The Recommendations/Observations, which have been accepted by the Government:
Para Nos. 3.2.4.3, 3.2.5.4, 3.2.6.3, 3.2.15.3, 3.2.16.3, 3.3.4.3, 3.3.5.3 and 3.3.6.3
(of One Hundred and Seventy Third Report)  Total Recommendations - 8
The Committee is pleased to note that the Ministry has accepted its recommendations
as mentioned in Chapter-I of the Report.
Chapter-II: The Recommendations/Observations which the Committee does not desire to pursue
in view of the Government’s replies: Para Nos. 3.2.7.3, 3.2.12.3, 3.2.13.3, 3.2.11.2
and 3.3.3.3 (ibid) Total Recommendations - 5
The Committee is convinced with the explanations furnished by the Ministry and,
therefore, does not want to pursue the recommendations further.
Chapter-III: The Recommendations/Observations in respect of which the Committee is not
satisfied with the replies of the Ministry: Para Nos. 3.1.1.6, 3.1.2.3, 3.1.3.3, 3.1.3.4,
3.1.4.2, 3.1.5.3, 3.1.6.3, 3.1.7.3, 3.2.1.4, 3.2.2.3, 3.2.3.3, 3.2.3.4, 3.2.5.5, 3.2.8.3,
3.2.16.4, 3.2.17.3, 3.2.18.3, 3.2.19.3, 3.3.1.3, 3.3.2.3, 3.3.7.3, 3.3.8.3 and 3.3.9.3
(ibid) Total Recommendations - 23
The Committee expresses its concern over the non-implementation of its
recommendations contained in Chapter-III and desires that the Ministry should
furnish convincing explanations in respect of those recommendations.
Chapter-IV: Recommendations/Observations in respect of which final replies of the Government
have not been received: Para Nos. 3.2.9.3, 3.2.10.3 and 3.2.14.7 (ibid)  Total
Recommendations - 3
In respect of three recommendations in Chapter-IV , the Ministry has either furnished
interim reply or couched its response in vague terms. Therefore, the Committee
desires that the Ministry should furnish pointed and detailed Action Taken Notes in
respect of the recommendations categorized in Chapter-IV in keeping with the spirit
of the recommendations.
3. The details of the A TRs have been analyzed in various Chapters in the succeeding chapters.

CHAPTE-I
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERV ATIONS WHICH HA VE BEEN ACCEPTED
BY THE GOVERNMENT
1.1 ONE TIME COMPENSATION
1.1.1 The Committee desires that one time compensation of ` 30 Lakh may be included in the
package and Ministry may ensure that the package is finalized.
                                                 (Para 3.2.4.3 of the 183 rd Report)
Action Taken
1.1.2 The Government of J&K has sent a proposal for one time settlement of displaced Persons
from PoJK, 1947 and Chhamb Displaced Persons of 1965 and 1971 wars to this Ministry. The
Ministry vide its letter dated 21.11.2014 has requested the State Government of J&K to send
certain more information with regard to the DPs of PoJK and DPs of Chhamb 1965 and 1971.
This Ministry has also requested the State Government to send one time proposal in respect of
WPRs also.
1.1.3 The Ministry of Home Affairs further informed the Committee that the required information
has not been furnished by the Government of J&K.  However, they have been again requested vide
letter dated 10.11.2015 to furnish the requisite information.
Further Observation
1.1.4 The Committee appreciates the initiative taken by the Ministry of Home Affairs for
seeking proposals for one time settlement of DPs from PoJK 1947 and Chhamb DPs of 1965
and 1971 as well WPRs and desires that all necessary action must be taken within a set
time frame, as all these affected persons continue to lead their lives under depression due
to extreme suffering. Any positive action on the part of the Government would be of great
satisfaction to them.
Recommendation
1.2 SLOW DISBURSAL OF COMPENSATION
1.2.1 The Committee expresses its deep concern that the payment of compensation in respect
of fund/package sanctioned in 2008 is being implemented at snail pace affecting the lives
of PoJK DPs. The process should have been completed much earlier. The Committee, therefore,
recommends that the Union Government must pursue the matter with the State Government
to expedite the implementation of the package without further delay. (Para 3.2.5.4)
Action Taken

Divisional Commissioner Jammu is in place for monitoring the progress of implementation of the

under the law. (Para 3.2.13.3)

CHAPTER - III
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERV ATIONS IN RESPECT OF WHICH REPLIES OF THE
GOVERNMENT HAVE NOT BEEN ACCEPTED BY THE COMMITTEE
Recommendation
3.1 WEST PAKISTANI REFUGEES (WPRS)
3.1.1 The Committee expresses its serious concern that the West Pakistani Refugees, who
are very much citizens of India and eligible for voting in Parliamentary elections do not
possess right to vote in the State legislature Assembly elections on the pretext that they
are not permanent residents of the State in terms of the J&K constitution. The Committee
feels that through they are living there for more than 60 years, they are not leading the
life of free citizens despite having voting rights for Parliament. This right has not earned
them any special benefits.  The Committee strongly recommends that the Central
Government must impress upon the State Government to consider, as a one time measure,
the demand of West Pakistani Refugees to grant them the status of permanent residents
of the State sympathetically so that they can live as state subject in a dignified way, with
all legal rights including right to vote in State Legislative Assembly. (Para 3.1.1.6)
Action Taken
3.1.2 The Government of India, on a number of occasions had taken up the issues relating to
the West Pakistani Refugees, including the conferment of Permanent Resident Status. The Union
Home Secretary vide his D.O. letter dated 07.11.2014 addressed to the Chief Secretary to the
Government of J&K has again requested for conferment of Permanent Resident Status to West
Pakistani Refugees settled in the State.
Further Recommendation
3.1.3 The Committee is aware that WPRs are not considered permanent residents of the
State of J&K in terms of the Constitution on the ground that WPRs does not  have
ownership of land i.e. sahib-e-jaidad of J&K in the year 1944, a pre-condition to acquire
a Permanent Residency Rights  but the fact that WPRs are living there since 1947
running from pillar to post in search of permanent source of livelihood.  Moreover, WPRs
arrived there even before enforcement of Article 370. The Committee observes that WPRs
are very much citizens of India having voting rights in Parliamentary elections, therefore,
there is no reason as to why WPRs should not be given voting rights for State Assembly
elections particularly when the ruling establishment at the centre and State Government
at the time of partition advised WPRs to stay at border villages and made assurance to
them for a decent life.  The Committee, therefore, strongly recommends that there should
8

9
not be any hitch in proposing amendment to the constitution of J&K in favour of WPRs
conferring Permanent Residence Certificate and voting rights for State Legislative
Assembly election in J&K. The Ministry of Home Affairs must pursue the matter with the
State Government.
Recommendation
3.2 PROVISION OF STATE GOVERNMENT JOBS
3.2.1 The Committee feels that once the permanent resident right is granted to West
Pakistani Refugees, all subsidiary benefits would automatically follow enabling them to lead
decent life.  The Committee, therefore, recommends that J&K constitution may be amended
for conferring the status of State Subject on the WPRs at the earliest. These people have
already suffered for more than 60 years and the issue brooks no delay.  The Committee
also recommends that pending final decision in the matter, a temporary waiver may be
made for admission of the children in the professional institutions. (Para 3.1.2.3)

3.2.2 The State Government has been requested that pending conferment of Permanent Resident
Status to the WPRs, a temporary waiver may be made for the admission of the children in the
professional institutions in the State. As already requested vide this Ministry’s letter dated
07.01.2015, the State Government must issue Domicile Certificates to the WPRs
3.2.3 The Ministry of Home Affairs vide its communication dated 4
th December, 2015 apprised the
Committee that State Government of J&K has not yet replied in this regard. They have again been
requested vide this Ministry’s letter dated 29.07.2015 and 10.11.2015 for furnishing action taken
report.
Further Recommendation
3.2.4 The Committee strongly reiterate its recommendation that pending conferment of
Permanent Resident Status to the WPRs, a temporary waiver may be made for admission
of the children in the professional institutions in the State.

WEST PAKISTANI REFUGEES (WPRs)
The Committee is aware that WPRs are not considered permanent residents of the State of
J&K in terms of the Constitution on the ground that WPRs does not  have ownership of land i.e
sahib-e-jaidad of J&K in the year 1944, a pre-condition to acquire a Permanent Residency Rights
but the fact that WPRs are living there since 1947 running from pillar to post in search of permanent
source of livelihood.  Moreover, WPRs arrived there even before enforcement of Article 370. The
Committee observes that WPRs are very much citizens of India having voting rights in Parliamentary
elections, therefore, there is no reason as to why WPRs should not be given voting rights for State
Assembly elections particularly when the ruling establishment at the centre and State Government
at the time of partition advised WPRs to stay at border villages and made assurance to them for a
decent life.  The Committee feels that there should not be any hitch in proposing amendment to the
constitution of J&K in favour of WPRs conferring Permanent Residence Certificate and voting
rights for State Legislative Assembly election in J&K. The Ministry of Home Affairs may pursue
the matter with the State Government. (Para 3.1.3)

INTRODUCTION
I, the Chairman of the Department-related Parliamentary Standing Committee on Home
Affairs, having been authorized by the Committee to submit the Report on its behalf, do hereby
present this One Hundred Ninety Fourth Report on Action Taken by Government on the
observations/recommendations contained in the One Hundred and Seventy Third Report on the
Strengthening of the working of the Ministry of DoNER for effective implementation of Policies,
Programmes, Schemes and Projects meant for North Eastern Region.
2. The One Hundred and Seventy Third Report of the Department-related Parliamentary
Standing Committee on Home Affairs was presented/laid to the Rajya Sabha and on the Table of the
Lok Sabha on 29th August, 2013. After presentation of the Report, the copies thereof were sent
to the Ministry of DoNER requesting them to furnish Action Taken Notes on the recommendations
of the Committee contained in the Report. The Action Taken Notes thereon were received from the
Ministry of DoNER on 22nd September, 2014. Based on the ATN the Secretariat forwarded a
Questionnaire to the Ministry of DoNER and the replies thereon were received.
3. The Committee visited the States of Assam, Meghalaya and Manipur from 25th to 29th May,
2015 for on-the-spot assessment of action taken on the recommendations contained in 173rd Report.
During the visit, the Committee held discussions with the Chief Secretaries and other officers of
the State Governments of Assam, Meghalaya and Manipur including local/district administrations and
other stakeholders on development projects in North-East Region.
4. The Committee in its meeting held on 29th June, 2015 decided to hear Chief Secretaries of
remaining five North Eastern States in Delhi which could not be heard during the aforesaid visit.
Accordingly, the Committee, in its meeting held on 27th July, 2015 heard the Secretary, Ministry
of DoNER along with the representatives of States viz. Arunachal Pradesh, Mizoram, Nagaland,
Sikkim and Tripura in Delhi itself. In the said meeting, the Committee, after a detailed assessment,
observed that the Ministry of DoNER has furnished superfluous, evasive and unsatisfactory response
to 31 recommendations out of a total of 49 recommendations as contained in 173rd Report. The
Committee observed that the Ministry of DoNER responded to six recommendations were found to
be incomplete and unsatisfactory. The Committee further observed that with regard to eight
recommendations of the Committee, the Ministry of DoNER just responded by indicating ‘noted for
compliance’ and while six recommendations were communicated to the other agencies without any
follow up action and eleven recommendations of the Committee were without exclusive response.
The Committee thereon directed the Secretary, Ministry of DoNER to hold detailed discussions with
State Governments and other Central Ministries and Departments and furnish revised action taken
notes to the Committee for examination and consideration.  The Ministry of DoNER furnished the
revised action taken notes on 14th August, 2015 after holding detailed discussion on 3rd August,
2015 with the representatives of North Eastern States.
5. The Minister of DoNER laid the statement on the status of implementation of the
recommendations contained in the said Report of the Committee on the Table of Lok Sabha on
(iii)

17th December, 2014 and Rajya Sabha on 18th December, 2014, pursuant to the Chairman, Rajya
Sabha’s Direction dated 24th September, 2004.
6. The present report has been prepared on the basis of revised action taken notes in the
backdrop of Committee’s meeting on 27th July, 2015 and the direction given by the Committee to
the Ministry of DoNER in the said meeting.
7. The Committee considered the draft One Hundred and Ninety Fourth Report and adopted the
same at its meeting held on 18 December, 2015.
