CHAPTER-I
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS WHICH HAVE BEEN ACCEPTED BY THE
GOVERNMENT
1.0 After hearing the views of various stakeholders viz. Ministry of DoNER, line Ministries,
representatives of North Eastern State Governments, Secretary, Department of Expenditure, Secretary,
Planning Commission and Cabinet Secretary on the subject, the Committee has arrived at the following
conclusions observations/ recommendations.
Recommendation
1.1 AVOIDANCE OF PROCEDURAL DELAY
1.1.1 From the evidence available, the Committee takes note of the fact that the major drawback in
the timely implementation and completion of the projects lies in the procedural delay. The Committee
is of the view that in order to give fillip to the development process in the region, the whole
Government machinery involving both the Central Government and State Governments need to pull up
their socks right from the stage of conceptualisation of schemes, allocation of funds, formulation of
DPRs, technical vetting of DPRs, obtaining environment/forest clearances to actual take-off of projects
on ground involving land acquisition, capacity building, conducive law and order situation, etc. This
requires a well balanced planning, good coordination between various agencies and time bound
clearances/rejections of projects. The Committee, therefore, recommends that a robust monitoring
mechanism should be put in place so that procedural delays at every stage of the projects are brought
down to minimum level, though ideal situation would be to remove all delays.
                                                 (Para 5.2.1 of the 173rd Report)
Action Taken
1.1.2 In pursuance of the directions given by Department-related Parliamentary Standing Committee
on Home Affairs, in its meeting held  on 27/07/2015, detailed discussions were held with the NE States
on 03/08/2015 through video conferencing so as to put in place a simplified procedure for expeditious
processing/execution of projects  under the NLCPR scheme. After  consultations and after examination
of feasibility, the following simplified procedure, which includes pre as well as post sanction of the
projects,  is proposed to be put in place so as to remove the bottlenecks and delays in the timely
completion of the projects:-
(i) The NE States to submit Priority Lists by September of the year for the next financial
year commencing from this year itself.
(ii) The normative allocation for the States will be intimated well in advance based on past
years’ trend after taking account of their infrastructure development indices, absorption
capacity as shown in pending projects and after accommodating needs for ongoing and
retained projects.
2

3
(iii) A project should be at a single location and should not a composite of several locations
as already specified in the Guidelines of NLCPR.
(iv) Priority List should be continuous and in a running format (No sector-wise, district-wise
categorisation of projects should be in the Priority List).
(v) The total value of projects included in the Priority List should not exceed 1.5 times of
the total normative allocation so intimated.
(vi) Projects exceeding 1.5 times of the allocation shall be summarily rejected.
(vii) The current specification in guidelines for reserving 25% of new projects for backward
areas is vague and will be specified as intended for Autonomous Territorial/District
Councils.
(viii) The concept paper for each project should clearly specify if the expenditure is to be
incurred on creating public assets, the nature of landholding, Government control and
management etc.
(ix) Chief Secretary/Planning Secretary/Departmental Secretary (when concerned) shall alone
attend the meeting of the NLCPR Committee, convened for initial screening of concept
papers and later for sanction of finalised DPRs of the projects included for the State. In
case these officers are unable to attend the meeting, another authorised representative,
who is able to take on the spot decisions, may alone attend the meeting.  In case the
authorised representative is unable to satisfactorily answer the queries of the Committee,
the project shall be rejected as unsupported and the funds diverted to next in priority or
to approved projects of other States.
(x) Once the project(s) are cleared, the States will be invariably (by default) required to
submit DPRs within a period of two months. In case more time is sought by the State
at the time of approval of concept, such time not exceeding two months beyond the
default period shall be given.
(xi) DPRs should invariably include all the mandatory certificates viz. Environment and forest
clearance, availability of land, free from encumbrances,  non-duplication certificate and
availability of stone and sand quarry in the proximity of the project (in case of road
projects) etc.
(xii) The DPRs should be prepared as per the check-list prescribed by respective line Ministries
and on standard software for which the Ministry will arrange training/workshops for the
State Government officials and for potential vendors nominated by States as part of the
Ministry’s Vendor Development efforts.
(xiii) During the consultation process, many State Governments requested that the cost of
preparation of DPRs may be included in the project cost. In response to query by
Secretary, DoNER with regard to the cost incurred by the States on preparation of DPR,
the State representatives assured him that they would advise the same shortly after
consultations. After receiving response from all NE State Governments, the same shall be
considered suitably for incorporating the costs of soil testing for buildings and bridges and
DPR preparation in the NLCPR guidelines.

4
(xiv) The State shall also certify that these projects have not been taken up or proposed to be
taken with any other funding mechanism in the past or during the current financial year.
(xv) On the receipt of DPRs, Technical Wing of Ministry of DoNER will carry out  preliminary
scrutiny. The consolidated queries of Technical Wing, if any, shall be circulated, online/
through e-mail, to the State Planning and Implementing Department within 15 days. In
case the reply is not received within the period of 15 days from receipt of query, it shall
be presumed that the State is not interested to pursue the project and the project will be
deleted within seven days thereafter without any further notice.
(xvi) On receipt of reply to the queries raised by the Technical Wing, the DPRs will be sent
to the vetting agency/line Ministries, with the request to vet the DPRs. The vetting agency
shall raise consolidated queries, if any, which will be forwarded to the State Government
through Ministry, which will be required to furnish replies to the same within a period of
15 days. If these queries are not settled within 15 days of communication, the State
Government will be given another 15 days for furnishing replies to the query from the
vetting agency, failing which it will presumed that the State is not interested to pursue the
project and the said project will stand rejected. However, if the State Government finds
it difficult to collect data for a reply and gives cogent and substantial reasons, further time
of up to 30 days may be provided and not beyond.
(xvii) Vetting agency will give techno-economic vetting of the projects within one month from
receipt of replies to the consolidated queries within a period one month. In case any further
query is raised because of unsatisfactory replies or issues arising, these should be settled
before or on the date the project is placed for sanction before the Screening Committee.
(xviii) The line Ministries/NITI Aayog/NEC will be approached in parallel for non-duplication
certificates and for certifying if the project is fit for gap funding. The line Ministries/NITI
Aayog/NEC shall give their comments/observations within one month else it will be
presumed to be clear for non-duplication and gap funding angle. In any event, these views
shall be finally provided at the time of project sanctions.
(xix) NLCPR Committee meeting shall be convened periodically to consider sanctioning of the
cleared projects, duly vetted by the vetting agency and will also record the information/
views on non-duplication and gap funding character.
(xx) Release of funds:
     States laid great priority on streamlining the release of funds by the Ministry.
Therefore, after sanction of the project by the inter-ministerial NLCPR Committee, the
administrative and financial sanction shall be issued after following the laid down
procedures. Tendering process shall be finalised within two months by following
transparent process of bidding and Work Order issued. A copy of the tender shall
mandatorily also be placed on the NEC and NLCPR websites. Ministry of DoNER would
release funds in three instalments comprising 30%, 50% and 20%.
Release of first installment of funds:  30 % of the central share i.e. 90% of the total
approved cost of the project, shall be released along with administrative and financial
sanction.

5
Release of second installment of funds:  50% of the central share subject the condition
that 50 % of the funds released as first instalment has been utilised by the State for the
project and commensurate physical progress.
Release of third and final installment of funds: 20% of the central share subject to
the condition that 90% of the released amount, including full State share of 10% stands
utilised and  on achievement of 70% of physical progress of the project.
(xxi) States shall release funds to the implementing agency within a period of 15 days from
receipt from this Ministry. A copy of the release order shall be uploaded on the NLCPR
website and/or sent to the Ministry and will be taken note of for further releases in this
and other projects of the State as an instance of diversion of funds.
(xxii) In case of delayed projects, not more than two extensions shall be given, with overall
cumulative ceiling of one and half years (two working seasons) from the original date
of completion of the project. Reasons for delay shall be approved by Principal Secretary/
Secretary, Planning, on the recommendations of Secretary of the Implementing
Department. In the event that the project remains incomplete, the State may retain the
projects for pursuit by themselves so that the Ministry may transfer the funds to other
projects selected for the States. In case the delay is on account of reasonable
justification acceptable to the Ministry, this requirement may be waived on a case to
case basis.
1.1.3 On the issue of expeditious implementation of programmes/schemes, the Secretary, Ministry of
DoNER apprised the Committee during its meeting held on 27th July, 2015 as under:-
“ On expeditious implementation, ...., we have advanced the timeline. Last year, we had the
Committee meeting for approving projects in November, but this year, we are having it in
September. We have already asked the States to give the priority list in September .....and they
come with the DPRs. They take some time to prepare the DPRs. They come back to us, we
sanction it, and then it goes on with that, .... The idea is that they don’t miss a season. The
working season is only from September to March-April. Therefore that season should not be
missed. After a project is sanctioned, they tender it and all that, and they will be ready for the
next season.”
1.1.4 In regard to use of software in preparation of detailed project report, the Secretary, Ministry
of DoNER stated as under:-
“ we have written to the States to use software for the preparation of DPRs so that there is
no occasion to see that once a DPR is approved and sanctioned and the funds are released,
the Project Officer should not suddenly discover that the project parameters, the ground depth,
the hill slopes or whatever are different from what were mentioned in the DPR and, therefore,
it is not feasible to implement it. Therefore, we have told them to use software, go by realistic
field parameters and then send us the DPR. ....... We have also asked our contractors – now
we have appointed one CPSU as a contractor for below 
` 50 crores projects and another for
above ` 50 crores projects – to use the software to vet the DPRs, and this is likely to lead to
efficiency.”

6
1.1.5 As reg ards, the procedural delay in vetting of the DPRs, the Secretary, Ministry of DoNER
explained the action taken by the Ministry as under:-
“ The vetting of  DPRs can be expedited only if there is a common agreed system of developing
the DPRs, and that common system is possible through use of common softwares.  There are
softwares available in the market, which are specifically utilized for such purposes — for
building roads and bridges.  It is used in all the large projects all over the country and across
the world also.  This is easily available even in the North-Eastern Region.   So, that is what
we feel is a method of having a commonality in approach for preparing DPRs so that it can
be prepared fast and also vetted fast... on the issue of enhancing transparency,  we are
developing a software... But we are preparing a software with the help of NIC on the uploading
of DPRs, on the transfer of information between  the DoNER and States, on issuing SMS alerts
on responses that are required from DoNER and from States, so that those SMS alerts go to the
concerned officer.  And, if the concerned officer does not take action, it goes to the next higher
level officer  who is required to take action to ensure that expeditious processing of papers is
done.   This should enable the States to upload the inspection reports, current photos of the
site, digital photos of the site, and also enable  the public to see them, upload their own photos
if they so feel like  and also to write their comments. So, this will be a web-enabled software.”
1.1.6 Apprising the Committee of the need for the software and arrive at a common approach to the
issue of preparing DPR, the Secretary, Ministry of DoNER submitted before the Committee as under:-
“ When we have a software the State agencies that are responsible for preparing DPRs are
forced to go and look at the field situation before filling in the contents of the software.  It
is not possible to fill in the contents of the software with imaginary or table calculations.
Therefore, that kind of a discipline is being introduced by the process of a structure being
created for that purpose. That is the first point, ...  A DPR can, again, not be prepared by
the engineers.  What we have proposed is that the States should acquire the DPR.  It is also
possible to fund the acquisition of DPR through the NLCPR.  That is not a problem.  The more
important thing is, because it does not entail a very high cost, to train the engineers and the
concerned agency officers of the State Governments in the use of the DPR.  Secondly, there
has to be vendor development.  Since it is not going to be done by the State officers themselves,
the vendors who prepare the DPRs must be trained in the use of that software.  So, there has
to be both vendor development and engineers’ development programmes, which we are prepared
to fund.  We are discussing the issue with the States.  That is present position of the matter.
It takes some time. I appreciate the Committee’ s concern on this issue.”
1.1.7 The Secretary, Ministry of DoNER, replying to the queries of the Committee as to how the
existing mechanism ensures appointment of the representatives of the concerned State Government in
the NLCPR Committee, deposed before the Committee in its sitting held on 27
th July, 2015 as under:-
“... from the last year, we have ensured that the State Government representatives are invited whenever
projects are considered by the Committee. We have invited them and they have invariably attended
directly from the State or through their local representatives. So, that is the position and that has not
changed at all.  The State Government representative, therefore, is invited to be a member of the
Standing Committee. The Standing Committee, as such, will consist of only four members - from NITI

7
Aayog, from Home Affairs, from Expenditure and from our Ministry.  That is the position.  There is
also one member from the Ministry which is concerned with that particular subject.”
Further Recommendation
1.1.8 The Committee observes that in compliance with the Committee’s recommendation for
avoidance of procedural delay and direction given it its meeting held on 27 th July, 2015, the
Ministry of DoNER in tandem with the State Governments and the concerned line Ministries has
undertaken a number of measures from the stage of conceptualization of scheme, preparation
and submission of priority list, expeditious processing/execution of projects under NLCPR
scheme, setting detailed guidelines and simplification of procedures for preparing and
submission and vetting of DPRs, sanctioning, allocation and release of funds for timely
implementation and completion of projects.  The Committee, however, would like to be apprised
of perceptible outcome of the measures so undertaken on the ground level in the form of period
of time reduced in clearance of projects and its completion in comparison to pre and post
reforms phase on removal of all unnecessary procedural delays.  The kernel spirit of the
Committee’s recommendation made in para 5.2.1 of the Committee’s 173
rd Report is to give
fillip to developmental process in NER through procedural facilitation and timely implementation
of policies, programmes, schemes and projects meant for all round balanced development of the
region.
1.1.9 The Committee further recommends that the Ministry of DoNER should take up the
issue of revisiting the instant specification in guidelines for reserving 25% of new projects for
backward areas which is at present vague and therefore needs modification on the lines of
autonomous territorial/district council.
1.1.10 The Committee also recommends that the Ministry of DoNER should persuade the line
ministries to arrange training/workshops for the State Government officials and for potential
vendors nominated by States as part of the Ministry’s Vendor Development efforts.  The
Committee believes that such measures would enable the State Government officials for
preparation of DPRs with great specification and on rationale basis to take into account detailed
survey and baseline facts. The Committee further desires that the request of the State
Governments for incorporating the cost of preparation of DPRs in the project cost should be
considered at the earliest and the same may be laid down in the NLCPR guidelines.
1.1.11 The Committee observes that no guidelines have been set up on frequency of meeting
of the NLCPR Committee and timeline for consideration  and sanctioning of cleared projects.
Therefore, the Committee desires that the meeting of the NLCPR should be convened
periodically with a set time-frame, known to the State Governments so that requisite
information may be furnished to the NLCPR Committee well in advance.  Also, timelines for
consideration and sanctioning of projects should be let up to avoid delays on their part.
Recommendation
1.2.1 The Committee also takes note of the complaints of the State Governments that the comments/
queries/clarifications of the Line Ministries are not sought in one go rather they are sought in 2-3
installments which are then replied to by the State Governments to the Line Ministries through the
Ministry of DoNER.  The entire process takes about 1-2 years and sometimes more, for sanction of

8
projects after submission of the DPRs, thus resulting in time/cost escalation of the projects. The
Committee also notes the complaint of the States that except for prioritization of projects, the States
have no role in the process of selection of projects to be funded under NLCPR.  The sanction of the
projects would be expedited if the representatives of the State Government are invited to attend the
meetings held for sanctioning of the projects, to give clarifications on the spot. The Committee,
therefore, recommends that in order to address the problem of delays by the Line Ministries/Departments,
a strict time-frame should be given for clearing DPRs. The Committee also recommends that required
administrative mechanism, including inviting representative of the concerned State Governments in the
meetings for on the spot clarifications, may be put in place.  The Line Ministries should not take
long time in approval and sanctioning of DP Rs. The time Lines as are to be fixed, should be strictly
adhered to. (Para 5.3.2 ibid)
Action Taken
1.2.2 Timelines have been put in place for vetting of DPRs by the Line Ministries or the PSU engaged
for the purpose. It has been decided that the Technical Wing of the Ministry will scrutinise the DPRs
within 15 days of its receipt and raise consolidated queries, if any. The queries shall be forwarded,
electronically, to State Governments for suitable clarification/modification, in the DPRs, of so required.
The States shall be given 15 days’ time to furnish their replies to the Ministry of Development of North
Eastern Region. This will go a long way in reducing delays at various levels.
1.2.3 The following procedure will  take care of the concerns expressed by the Hon’ble Committee:-
1.2.4 The Ministry has engaged PSUs for expeditious vetting of DPRs submitted by the State
Governments. The following measures have also been taken to optimally reduce the time taken for
vetting of DPRs submitted by the State Governments:-
(a) On receipt of DPRs from the State Governments, the Technical Wing of the Ministry of
DoNER will do the preliminary scrutiny.  The consolidated  query, if any, of the Technical
Wing shall be given within 15 days to the Programme Division, which will be forwarded
online/through e-mail, to the State Planning and Implementing Department. In case the
reply is not received within the period of 15 days from receipt of query, it shall be
presumed that the State is not interested to pursue the project and the project will be
deleted within seven days thereafter without any further notice.
(b) On receipt of reply to the queries raised by the Technical Wing, the DPRs will be sent
to the vetting agency/Line Ministries, with the request to vet the DPRs. The vetting
agency shall raise consolidated queries, if any, which will be forwarded to the State
Government through Ministry, which will be required to furnish replies to the same within
a period of 15 days. If these queries are not settled within 15 days of communication,
the State Government will be given another 15 days for furnishing replies to the query
from the vetting agency, failing which it will presumed that the State is not interested to
pursue the project and the said project will stand rejected. However, if the State
Government finds it difficult to collect data for a reply and gives cogent and substantial
reasons, further time of up to 30 days may be provided and not beyond.
(c) V etting agency will give techno-economic vetting of the projects within one month from
receipt of replies to the consolidated queries within a period one month. In case any

9
further query is raised because of unsatisfactory replies or issues arising, these should be
settled before or on the date the project is placed for sanction before the Screening
Committee.
(d) The Line Ministries/NITI Aayog/NEC will be approached parallelly for non-duplication
certificates and for certifying if the project is fit for gap funding. The Line Ministries/NITI
Aayog/NEC shall give their comments/observations within one month else it will be
presumed to be clear for non-duplication and gap funding angle. In any event, these views
shall be finally provided at the time of project sanctions.
(e) NLCPR Committee meeting shall be convened periodically to consider sanctioning of the
cleared projects, duly vetted by the vetting agency.
Recommendation
1.3 REPRESENTATIVES FROM STATE GOVERNMENT IN NLCPR
1.3.1 The Committee agrees with the demand of the North Eastern State Governments that there
should be a representative of the State, possibly the Chief Secretary or the Commissioner/Secretary, in
charge Planning Department of the State in the NLCPR Committee for retention and sanctioning of
projects and recommends that necessary steps be taken to ensure representation of the concerned State
Governments in the NLCPR Committee. (Para 5.3.4 ibid)
Action Taken
1.3.2 Representatives of State Governments concerned are invariably invited to attend the meetings of
the inter-ministerial NLCPR Committee for retention and sanction of the projects taken up for funding
under the scheme of NLCPR. To further strengthen the procedure, it has been agreed that Chief
Secretary/Planning Secretary/Departmental Secretary (when concerned) shall alone attend the meeting of
the NLCPR Committee, convened for initial screening of concept papers and later for sanction of
finalised DPRs of the projects included for the State. In case these officers are unable to attend the
meeting, another authorised representative, who is able to take on the spot decisions, may alone attend
the meeting.  In case the authorised representative is unable to satisfactorily answer the queries of the
Committee, the project shall be rejected as unsupported and the funds diverted to next in priority or
to approved projects of other States.
Recommendation
1.4 CAPACITY CONSTRAINTS
1.4.1 The Committee finds that the State Governments have to do a lot of catching up as far as
capacity building is concerned.  The Committee takes note of the complaints regarding inadequate
investigations and project formulation which led to changes in scope and revision of drawings at later
stage. It also notes problems related to inappropriate and inadequate procurement and faulty contractual
management system. Poor selection of contractors due to low bids with no technical capability to handle
the project led to cost overruns, schedule delays, poor quality etc. The Committee also finds that in
some cases the project lengths are very large and there is lack of technical expertise in State PWDs
in implementing the projects. The Committee further observes that there is dearth of local contractors
with sound financial and technical capabilities and low participation of contractors from other parts

10
of the country in the tenders also. The Committee is, therefore, of the considered view that concerted
effort is required on the part of the Ministry of DoNER and Planning Commission to improve State
Governments’ capabilities for project preparation and execution. The Ministry of DoNER in consultation
with Finance Ministry and Planning Commission should chalk out a long-term plan for capacity
building of State Governments of NER keeping in mind huge infrastructure needs of the region. The
Committee also recommends that the Ministry of DoNER should extend technical and other related help
to the State PWDs to improve their technical capacities and execution capabilities. The State
Governments and Ministry of DoNER should also take necessary steps for assisting local contractors
to upgrade their skills. (Para 5.4.1 ibid)
Action Taken
1.4.2 It is proposed to enhance the technical and execution capabilities of the State agencies by
imparting training of their technical personnel, organising workshops etc.
Further Recommendation
1.4.3 The Committee may be apprised of the action plan prepared with regard to capacity
building i.e. technical and execution capabilities of State Government.
Recommendation
1.5 PROBLEMS RELATED TO LAW AND ORDER SITUATION
1.5.1 The Committee finds that the law and order situation is one of the biggest problems in NER
which is posing a threat to the projects by preventing them from taking off. The Committee has on
record the suggestion of Line Ministries that the local problems and law and order issues should be
addressed by State and local administrations to ensure smooth completion of projection. Agreeing with
the view of Line Ministries, the Committee suggests that all local issues including problems of law and
order should be addressed by the local administration and State Authorities.
(Para 5.5.1 ibid)
Action Taken
1.5.2 State Governments are responsible for the law and order situation and are expected to provide
conducive environment for execution of the projects.  Chief Secretaries of all the eight North Eastern
States have been requested to ensure safety of the personnel working at the respective work sites.
Recommendation
1.6 LACUNAE ON THE PART OF THE STATE GOVERNMENTS
1.6.1 The Committee is of the view that the onus of development in NER lies as much on the State
Governments as on the agencies of the Central Government. The Committee is constrained to express
its displeasure to find that the Line Ministries and State Governments pass the buck to each other while
facing bottlenecks during the course of implementation of projects for development. But, the need is
to exercise introspection. State Governments cannot get away just by pointing fingers towards the Centre
and vice-versa. The case in point is the 3,000 MW Debang Power Project to be executed by NHPC,
where  even holding of public hearings, which was one of the first things to happen, could not be
conducted because of law and order situation and had to be postponed 12 times. After a lot of

11
intervention by the Ministry of Power and the personal intervention of the Minister of Power, the public
hearing was conducted. Similar is the case with many projects which certainly hampered the process of
development in NER.
1.6.2 The Ministry of Surface Transport and Highways cited a case under Arunachal package for road
construction of 740 kms., in two packages—one of 300 plus kms. and the other of 440 kms.  But land
acquisition for these stretches could not be completed for a long period of two years.  Since the Ministry
had decided to award projects only when 90% of the land was available, the programmes could not
be executed for want of land acquisition.
1.6.3 Another case that has come to the notice of the Committee is that of a scheme of providing
100 per cent central assistance to the North-Eastern States for taking up river development works.
Apart from the National Waterway-2, that is, the Brahmaputra River , there are other river stretches also
which could be developed for cargo transportation.  The Committee is disappointed to note that
response or the initiative from the States of the North-Eastern Region is lacking. The Central
Government, on its own, engaged M/s. RITES to identify river stretches which could be developed for
such cargo transportation and RITES had identified 22 river stretches in all the States of North-Eastern
Region for development.  Those identified river stretches had been shared with the concerned State
Governments and they had been requested to send proposals for assistance.  However, so far, only three
proposals have been received, one of which had been sanctioned.  The Committee is of the opinion that
the North-Eastern States need to be more proactive in sending the proposals for development of these
river stretches for cargo transportation.
1.6.4 One more example that has come to the notice of the Committee is the case of fixed terminal
at Pandu which is supposed to be completed by June, 2014. Dedicated road connectivity has been
sanctioned at a cost of 
` 11 crore to connect National Highway-31 and for this, land was required from
the Railways.  The requisite amount had been paid but the land had not been transferred owing to
2,150 encroachments which are to be cleared by the State Government. The Committee was informed
that either the encroachment had to be removed or an alternative piece of land for an alternative
alignment has to be given. This dedicated connectivity from the Waterway Terminal to the National
Highway would be an essential requirement for smooth flow of cargo. The Committee observes that the
removal of encroachments by the concerned State Government at the earliest is the only option as there
is no other alignment possible.  In view of the above illustrations,  the Committee is of the firm view
that the Ministry of DoNER should play a pro-active role in resolving issues amongst Line Ministries
and State Governments for timely execution of projects and State Governments should also come
forward with their cooperation.  Unless States take initiative and cooperate, projects cannot take off
and development will continue to be hampered.
(Para 5.7.1, 5.7.2, 5.7.3 and 5.7.4)
Action Taken
1.6.5 Ministry of Development of North Eastern Region shares the recommendation that development
process in NER needs full cooperation between State Governments and agencies of Central
Government. State Government have been impressed upon to be more proactive in sending proposals
and taking initiative so that development process in the region does not hamper and also to hasten
process of land acquisition, wherever required. Ministry of Development of North Eastern Region has
taken due cognizance of the proactive role that is required to be played by it in resolving issues amongst

12
Line Ministries and State Governments for timely execution of the projects. Recognising the importance
of States’ cooperation, views of all stakeholders are now taken before deciding a policy. Changes in
policies are preceded by detailed stakeholder consultations.  In pursuance of this shift in policy, a Chief
Ministers’ Conference was organized on 21 & 22
nd August at Guwahati in Assam where aspirations of
the NE people were articulated by the States and Ministry of DoNER is now engaged in putting in place
appropriate mechanism for converting these into reality.
1.6.6 In the said C onference of the Chief Ministers of the North Eastern Region, the dignitaries, the
State Governments and the Task Groups constituted during the Conference presented and shared their
views on the state of development of transport connectivity, such as Rail, Road, Air and Waterways
in North Eastern Region; the factors/issues impeding the development of transport network and road-
map/vision for improvement thereof within North Eastern Region and of the region with other parts of
the country/adjoining countries. The conference also shared the view that dismal state of transport
network in North Eastern Region is one of prime factors impeding growth and development in the
region.  To address the issue, Ministry of DoNER has constituted a inter-ministerial Working Group on
development of transport network in North Eastern Region with the following terms and reference:-
(i) to assess and map the present state of development of transport network in North Eastern
Region;
(ii) to make recommendations for coordinated development, roadmap and vision of various
transport network/sectors in North Eastern Region in medium and long terms;
(iii) to make recommendations with regard to action plan, strategy and modalities for
implementation of its recommendations;
(iv) to identify issues, concern areas and challenges;
(v) to crystallize approach and make recommendations to address issues, concern areas and
challenges;
Further Recommendation
1.6.7 The Committee would like to be apprised of the recommendations of inter-ministerial
working group on development of transport network in North Eastern Region alongwith action
taken by the Government thereon.  The Committee would further desire to know about
progress on 3000 MW Debang Power Project that was to be executed by NHPC, Arunachal
Package for road construction of 740 km., decision granting scheme of providing 100% central
assistance to NER states for taking up river development works.
Recommendation
1.7 TELECOM SECTOR
1.7.1 The Committee takes note of the poor telecom connectivity in North-East.  The telecom system
is linear which if broken at a point disturbs the whole segment. The Committee agreeing with the
suggestion of the Department of Telecommunications, recommends that provision of having ducts
alongside the roads is a good suggestion and it should be made mandatory for road works not only
in NER but also in the whole country so that no OFC is damaged on account of road works. The
Committee recommends that the existing infrastructure available with organizations like Power Grid

13
Corporation, Railtel etc. as well as State Governments should provide Right of Way at a reasonable
cost for better connectivity in the region. The Committee also notes that the Department of
Telecommunications had suggested an alternative connection from Tripura to Akhora in Bangladesh to
provide an alternative path and the matter is being negotiated through the Ministry of External Affair
Ministry. The Committee desires that the negotiations in this regard may be concluded at the earliest
to ensure communication connectivity to the North East Region with the country.
1.7.2 The Committee also notes that the Power Grid Corporation is not ready to lend a pair of fibre
in the cable going on the transmission lines on cost sharing basis as it is rather interested in giving
the bandwidth on lease commercially to earn more money.  The matter had been brought to the notice
of the PMO and Cabinet Secretary, but with no avail.  The Committee in this connection would like
to impress upon the Government that connectivity to the North East Region should not be viewed solely
on commercial lines to make profit as it is for the national cause. The Committee therefore recommends
that the PMO and Cabinet Secretary should intervene in the matter to sort out the issue at the earliest.
1.7.3 As mentioned earlier, losses can make any activity unsustainable for long period and keeping
in mind that the viability gap funding is needed to ensure commercial feasibility for regular provision
of telecommunication services in North East, the Committee recommends that the issue of viability gap
funding may be examined and may be provided for regular provision of telecommunication services in
North East. (Paras 5.9.1, 5.9.2 & 5.9.3 ibid)
Action Taken
1.7.4 Use of OPGW (Optical Ground Wire) of PGCIL’s Transmission lines for setting alternate
telecommunications network:- MOU signed between BSNL and PGCIL in June, 2014 to augment
broadband capacities at 20 places on payment basis.  Implementation period is 12-18 months. Telecom
connectivity in border areas - MHA has agreed to fund strengthening of telecom services in border area
in general and BSF posts in particular for which survey is under progress. This will also address the
problem of use of mobile network of neighbouring countries in border areas. Setting of utility duct
along National Highways (as done in Mumbai - Pune Expressway) - Utility duct provisioning along NH
from Guwahati to Shillong is being taken up by MORTH on pilot basis. Alternate transmission
connectivity between Kolkata and Tripura via Dhaka: Dhaka - Akhaura - Agartala OF link (10G) - is
under discussion. Setting up International internet gateway at Agartala (for better and reliable internet
connectivity) through cox bazar by using existing submarine cable of BSCCL- is also under discussion.
Based on the request of the Department of Telecom, Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI)
issued Recommendations on “Improving Telecom Services in North-Eastern States: An Investment
Plan”, dated 26
th September, 2013.  In its meeting held on 13.06.2014, the Telecom Commission
approved a proposal to implement the comprehensive telecom development plan at an estimated project
cost of ` 5336.18 crores. Union Cabinet has since approved the “Comprehensive Development Plan for
NER” on 15/09/2014. Main thrust areas identified for improvement and augmentation of telecom
services in North-Eastern Region (NER) are:-
(i) to provide 2G  mobile coverage in identified uncovered villages.
(ii) to provide seamless 2G mobile coverage along the National Highways in NER.
(iii) to ensure reliability of and redundancy in the transmission network at State capitals and
district headquarters in NER.

14
1.7.5 Nat ional Optical Fibre Network (NOFN):  NOFN project is planned to connect all Gram
Panchayats (approx. 2.5 lakh) in the country including those in the North Eastern Region (inclusive of
Sikkim) through optical fibre utilizing existing fibers of Public Sector Undertakings (PSUs) and laying
incremental fiber wherever necessary to bridge the connectivity gap between Gram Panchayats (GPs)
and Blocks, for providing broadband connectivity. NOFN project is being executed by BSNL (in Sikkim
and Assam) and Rail Tel (in Arunachal Pradesh, Manipur, Meghalaya, Mizoram, Nagaland and Tripura).
NOFN will deliver bandwidth of 100 Mbps at each Gram Panchayat. The roll-out of NOFN is planned
to be completed by 31.03.2017.
Recommendation
1.8 AIR CONNECTIVITY
1.8.1 The Committee is aware of the fact that airports in the region have certain problems with regard
to the night landing facilities.  The region has got all the ground base facilities and visual facilities.
However, some instrument landing facilities are required to be provided in some States. The Committee
has been assured that by end of the financial year 2013-14, all these North-Eastern airports will be
equipped with instrument-related night landing facility. The Committee desires that there may not be any
delay in this regard. (Paras 5.10.1 ibid)
Action Taken
1.8.2 For improving the air connectivity in North East Region, AAI had taken up a number of
infrastructure development works at various airports in the past decade and is planning number of
development works in coming years. The objective is to make Guwahati as Inter-Regional Hub and
Agartala, Dibrugarh and Imphal as Intra-Regional Hubs.
1.8.3 Three Greenfield airports are also considered to be developed in NE Region viz. Sikkim
(Pakyong), Arunachal Pradesh (Itanagar) and Nagaland (Site not finalized).
There are twelve non-operational airports in the region out of which there is proposal to develop and
operationalise eight – Along, Daparizo, Pasighat, Tezu and Ziro in Arunachal Pradesh, Tura in
Meghalaya, Rupsi in Assam and Kailashahar in Tripura.
1.8.4 Night landing facilities and clearance for night operation are available for Agartala,  Dibrugarh,
Dimapur, Guwahati, Imphal and Lilabari airports out of which night operations are there at Agartala,
Guwahati and Imphal. For Jorhat, Silchar and Tezpur Airports, IAF has been requested for providing
night landing facilities and approvals for night operation. For development of the airports at Lengpui and
Tura, AAI has been instructed to take over the airports from the concerned State Governments.

1.9 FINANCIAL SUPPORT TO AIRPORTS IN NE
1.9.1 Attention of the Committee has also been drawn to the drawback in the Route Disbursal
Guidelines, under which airlines are obliged to deploy 10 per cent of their capacity, which they are

17
operating on the metro routes, to the North-East and however, by taking advantage of the drawback,
they are operating a lot of services to Guwahati and Bagdogra and the main problem of the
connectivity within the North-East is still very much there, thus defeating the very purpose of the
Guidelines in letter and spirit. It has been suggested that there may be Airport Connectivity Guidelines
(ACG) and Code Sharing with national and regional airlines to overcome this problem. The Committee
recommends that the matter of having Airport Connectivity Guidelines (ACG) and Code Sharing with
national and regional airlines may be examined earnestly to ensure air connectivity to all parts of the
North East, and not just Guwahati and Bagdogra in the name of obligation under Route Disbursal
Guidelines.  The Committee also received a suggestion that Ministry of DoNER/NEC should give 100%
financial support as all the airports are making losses. The Committee recommends that this suggestion
of Ministry of Civil Aviation may be examined. (Para 5.10.2)
Action Taken
1.9.2 Subsidy to Alliance Air based on viability gap for providing increased air connectivity in North
Eastern Region: A meeting of Expenditure Finance Committee (EFC) on 13.08.2014 under the
Chairmanship of Secretary, DoNER recommended for sanction the scheme of NEC, “Providing Air
Connectivity in North Eastern Region” at ` 124.12 crore to be implemented during 2014-15 and 2015-16.
Administrative approval for the scheme was issued on 25
th August 2014. Under scheme, North Eastern
Council (NEC) provides subsidy to Alliance Air based on viability gap (based on total cost minus
revenue formula) for providing air connectivity to unconnected/inadequately connected airports in NER,
namely, Lilabari, Shillong, Silchar and Tezpur, to begin with. Alliance Air Ltd. has commenced air
services connecting these airports with Guwahati/Kolkata. A provision that within the recommended cost
of ` 124.12 crore, new routes may be added or flight schedules and frequencies may be added, in
public interest, has been built into the scheme so that future changes in air connectivity requirements
can be met from the scheme.
1.9.3 Due to inadequate Gross Budgetary Support (GBS) received by the Ministry of DoNER, the
Ministry/NEC regrets its inability to extend 100% financial support to airports in NER.
Further Recommendation
1.9.4 The Committee notes the inability of DoNER/NEC to provide 100% financial support to
airports in NE.  The Ministry of Finance may look into this aspect and find a way out for the
problem.
Recommendation
1.10 CONSTITUTION OF EMPOWERED GROUP OF MINISTERS TO REVIEW KEY
INFRASTRUCTURE PROGRAMMES

review key infrastructural projects. The Committee notes that the Government is already seized of the

CHAPTER-II
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS ON WHICH THE COMMITTEE DOES NOT DESIRE
TO PURSUE THE MATTER IN VIEW OF THE GOVERNMENT’S REPLY
Recommendation
2.1 Detailed Project Reports (DPRs)
2.1.1 The Committee observes that the State Governments do not have sufficient wherewithal to make
proper analysis and investigations. This has been agreed by all sides. Because of this, most of the DPRs
submitted by the State Governments entail a lot of short comings. The Ministry of DoNER has to send
them to the States back again and again for clarifications and sometimes advise the States that they
should outsource this work so that State Governments can have inputs of experts in DPRs. The State
Governments on the other hand suggested for the preparation of DPRs only after the projects are
retained by the Ministry as it involves huge expenditure to prepare DPRs. The State Governments
suggested that the Ministry of DoNER should accept the idea of concept papers for proposing projects
under NLCPR and only after retention, the specific details in the form of DPRs may be called for . The
Committee is of the view that the Ministry of DoNER and Planning Commission should look into the
feasibility of the suggestion of the State Governments or else the State Governments should outsource
their DPRs to improve the quality. The Committee, therefore, recommends that the Ministry of DoNER
in consultation with Planning Commission and the State Governments should workout the best course
in this regard so that unnecessary delays do not take place at the DPR stage itself.
2.1.2 The Committee takes note of the complaint of the line Ministries that while preparing DPRs,
the State Governments/agencies do not make proper survey and study of the local situation.  This leads
to cost escalation many a time.  This calls for development of efficient agencies for preparing DPRs
and outsourcing DPRs to them. Ministry of DoNER should prepare a plan and for this purpose and
get it implemented by States. The Committee feels that if the above recommendation is implemented,
this can be taken care of. (Paras 5.3.1 and 5.3.2)
Action Taken
2.1.3 The recommendation made by the Hon’ble Committee that the State Governments may be asked
to submit DPRs only after retention of projects based on the Concept Papers submitted by them, is
already in vogue. State Governments have also been advised to submit, alongwith with DPRs, all the
mandatory certificates viz. Environment and forest clearance, availability of land free from all
encumbrances,  non-duplication certificate and location of stone quarry, in case of road projects.  This
will considerably speed up the process of sanction and release. The Ministry has engaged PSUs for
expeditious vetting of DPRs submitted by the State Governments. The following measures have been
taken to optimally reduce the time taken for vetting of DPRs submitted by the State Governments:
(a) On receipt of DPRs from the State Governments, the Technical Wing of the Ministry of
DoNER will do the preliminary scrutiny. The consolidated  query, if any, of the Technical
Wing shall be given within 15 days to the Programme Division, which will be forwarded
22

23
online/through e-mail, to the State Planning and Implementing Department. In case the
reply is not received within the period of 15 days from receipt of query, it shall be
presumed that the State is not interested to pursue the project and the project will be
deleted within seven days thereafter without any further notice.
(b) On receipt of reply to the queries raised by the Technical Wing, the DPRs will be sent
to the vetting agency/line Ministries, with the request to vet the DPRs. The vetting agency
shall raise consolidated queries, if any, which will be forwarded to the State Government
through Ministry, which will be required to furnish replies to the same within a period of
15 days. If these queries are not settled within 15 days of communication, the State
Government will be given another 15 days for furnishing replies to the query from the
vetting agency, failing which it will presumed that the State is not interested to pursue the
project and the said project will stand rejected. However, if the State Government finds
it difficult to collect data for a reply and gives cogent and substantial reasons, further time
of up to 30 days may be provided and not beyond.
(c) Vetting agency will give techno-economic vetting of the projects within one month from
receipt of replies to the consolidated queries within a period one month. In case any further
query is raised because of unsatisfactory replies or issues arising, these should be settled
before or on the date the project is placed for sanction before the Screening Committee.
(d) The line Ministries/NITI Aayog/NEC will be approached in parallel for non-duplication
certificates and for certifying if the project is fit for gap funding. The line Ministries/NITI
Aayog/NEC shall give their comments/observations within one month else it will be
presumed to be clear for non-duplication and gap funding angle. In any event, these views
shall be finally provided at the time of project sanctions.
(e) NLCPR Committee meeting shall be convened periodically to consider sanctioning of the
cleared projects, duly vetted by the vetting agency.
2.1.4 Besides, the Ministry is in the process of developing through NIC, a Project Management
software for monitoring the implementation and execution of NLCPR funded projects.
Recommendation
2.2 ISSUES RELATED TO ENVIRONMENT/FOREST CLEARANCES
2.2.1 Regarding forest clearance at the State level and the Central level, the Committee finds that
time limits are generally not adhered to and they do not even have sub-limits. It appears that there is
no time limit for any particular agency to give the clearance. The Committee is, therefore, of the
opinion that the clearances should be given within the prescribed time limits and there should be sub-
limits for different stages. The time limit for the Central and State Governments and their concerned
agencies should be fixed and strictly adhered to.
2.2.2 The Committee further recommends that the Ministry of Environment and Forest should apply
different standards in the cases of strategically important projects such as the ones located on
international borders or near to it, as these locations are of strategic importance for the safety and
security of the country. The absence of such infrastructure will severely hamper the movement of
artillery and logistics in times of border tension.

24

the projects pending for environmental clearances and issue instructions to Ministry of Environment and

of DoNER may take initiative in this regard and take up with the State Governments.
(Paras 5.6.1, 5.6.2 and 5.6.3 )

2.4 KEEPING NLCPR FUNDS IN A REVOLVING FUND
2.4.1 Regarding the suggestion that NLCPR funds should be kept in a Revolving Fund to be operated
by DoNER, and it should  be made available to the States based on their demand and capacity without
being constrained by yearly budgetary ceilings, the Committee agrees with the view of the Finance
Ministry that creating a Revolving Fund for NLCPR would practically be not feasible. It also agrees
with the view that such funds being made available based on demand and capacity of States without
constraint of yearly budgetary ceilings would have implications on Government of India finances,
adversely affecting fiscal deficit, etc., besides, withdrawals from such funds , in Public Account, would
also require Parliamentary approval. Keeping in mind such practical difficulties, the Committee
recommends that a better course of action is required to make line Ministries spend the mandatory

sensitize Ministries to spend 10% GBS meant for NE States more quickly and effectively.
(Para 5.17.1)

25
Action Taken

objective of earmarking of at least 10% of GBS of the ministries is that each ministry should utilise

and balanced development of the region.
2.4.3 It is observed that wherever schematic guidelines of programmes are not suitable for the North
East utilisation of funds under such programmes invariably goes down resulting in transfer of unutilised
balance to the non-lapsable “notional pool”. In many cases the concerned ministries are also asking for
exemption of such schemes from earmarking for NER. The stand taken by Ministry of DoNER in such

have also positively responded to M/o DoNER’s suggestion and changed the guidelines relating to

habitations was brought down from initial 500 persons to 250 persons for the North East. Similarly,
M/o Textiles formulated an umbrella scheme, namely, “North East Region Textile Promotion Scheme
(NERTPS)” to cover various sub-schemes for the North East. Subsequently, utilisation of funds for the
north east by the Ministry of Textiles is quite encouraging. There are number of schemes for which
funding pattern was changed for better utilisation.
2.4.4 Apart from sensitising the non-exempted Ministries and the States of North East, for better
utilisation of funds, Ministry of DoNER and NEC is focusing on the monitoring of utilisation on regular
basis. Web based information of the Ministry of Finance on schematic fund releases is a good source
of information on day to day monitoring and timely intervention by the ministries and the States. NEC
has already initiated sectoral programme reviews at the State level based on available information.
Recommendation
2.5 FINANCING PATTERN OF SCHEMES UNDER NLCPR
2.5.1 Most of the representatives of the State Governments expressed before the Committee their
inability to finance State share of 10 percent under NLCPR Schemes. Their grievance is that NLCPR
financing pattern of 90% grant and 10% loan implied borrowing of huge amounts of funds from open
markets to finance projects, thus proving a burden for the States’ finances. The State Governments felt
that the requirement of 10% loan component should be done away with so that the heavy financial
burden of the State can be eased. Various Centrally Sponsored Schemes (CSS) administered by various
Central Ministries have varied funding patterns of 50:50, 75:25, 80:20, 90:10, and 100:00 etc. The
State Governments were of the view that since the requirement of the State share is met out of the
limited untied Plan Fund, the States are left with less funds for implementation of their own prioritised
schemes and projects. The State Governments, therefore, requested for full funding of the schemes/
projects.  The Committee, however, is not in agreement with the views of the State Governments and
is of the considered view that the State Governments should also show their involvement/interest/
ownership/commitment/participation in the implementation and execution  of the projects which could
only be ensured with their being financial  stakeholder in the projects. However, wherever the cost

26
escalation increases the share of the State, the Ministry of DoNER and Planning Commission may
consider the component of cost escalation to reduce the financial burden on the States.
(Para 5.18.1)
Action Taken
2.5.2 It is a fact that capacity to provide State share for a programme depend on the resource
position of the State as well as the funding pattern of various programmes implemented by the States.
It may be mentioned there is a drastic change in the pattern of resources flow to the States after the
14
th Finance Commission (FC) devolution. According to the Department of Expenditure, FC has
awarded devolution of Taxes @ 42% to the States in comparison to 32% recommended by the 13 th
FC. Further, the share of devolution of taxes to the North Eastern States, including Sikkim,
recommended by 14 th FC has been 7.91% as against 6.15% recommended by the 13 th FC. Therefore,
there will be significant enhancement of transfer of resources to NE States.  Apart from the Devolution
of Taxes, 14 th FC has recommended Revenue Deficit Grant to the eligible States.
2.5.3 However, S tates of NE have expressed their reservations about the enhancement in the
resources flow. According to them Central Assistance provided through certain plan programmes (like
Special Plan Assistance, Special Central Assistance, Normal Central Assistance and other block grant
programmes excluding NEC, NLCPR and ACA for EAP) has been de-linked from plan and subsumed
in the 14
th FC award resulting in shrinkage in the total flow of resources. States have also expressed
concern about likely change in the funding pattern of certain Centrally Sponsored Schemes (CSS) and
committed liabilities of the delinked programmes. Presently, NITI Aayog has constituted a Sub-group
for consultation with the States on Rationalisation of CSS and funding pattern. The concerns expressed

to accommodating cost escalation of the sanctioned scheme in the scheme itself, it may be mentioned

approved cost by the Ministry of DoNER and the State Government concerned as per the existing
pattern of funding

27
NEC and NLCPR outlays were kept beyond the ambit of State Plan or agree to this regime only if the

region and financial outlays under the Plan for the Region as a whole, as determined by the State

2.6.2 The Committee also notes the Comments of the Planning Commission that the inclusion of NEC

th Plan.

Recommendation
2.7 Delay in Land Acquisition and Inclusion of Land Cost in Projects.
2.7.1 The Committee notes that most projects have a precondition that the land should be made
available by the State Governments. However, North Eastern State Governments are reluctant on this
part on the ground that with increasing pressure on land and loss of land due to erosion, it is becoming
increasingly difficult for the States to fulfill this criterion. At times, the land is available at unviable
locations. The State Governments viewed that Ministry of DoNER should incorporate the land cost in
the projects. It should also help NER States to procure land for projects given by other line Ministries.
The Committee came across the issue related to land acquisition, in Arunachal Pradesh, where public
hearing, the first and foremost procedure for land acquisition, had to be postponed twelve times and
finally was held after a lot of persuasions. The Committee agrees with the Cabinet Secretary that only
States ought to address the issue since the major projects are essentially executed through the State
PWDs.

` 31 crore each), whereas, sanction was approved for only the Phase II of
31 kms. after reduction of almost ` 10 crore from the detailed estimate of the DPR. The Committee
also notes another instance where only a small length out of the proposed road projects was retained,

of the technical vetting authority for DPRs of NLCPR projects is to examine the broad outline
feasibility and correctness of the DPR instead of raising observations on a particular drawing/
estimate being countersigned or not, or raising arbitrary observations. The Committee views that
undue delay in vetting of DPRs necessitates revision in Administrative and Financial approval
which finally delays completion of projects abnormally. The Committee recommends that the

Action Taken
3.7.3 The services of the Technical Wing will be utilised for preliminary scrutiny of DPRs and

Governments. The following measures have also been taken to optimally reduce the time taken for
vetting of DPRs submitted by the State Governments:-
(a) On receipt of DPRs from the State Governments, the Technical Wing of the Ministry
of DoNER will do the preliminary scrutiny.  The consolidated  query, if any, of the
Technical Wing shall be given within 15 days to the Programme Division, which will
be forwarded online/through e-mail, to the State Planning and Implementing
Department. In case the reply is not received within the period of 15 days from
receipt of query, it shall be presumed that the State is not interested to pursue the
project and the project will be deleted within seven days thereafter without any further
notice.
(b) On receipt of reply to the queries raised by the Technical Wing, the DPRs will be sent
to the vetting agency/line Ministries, with the request to vet the DPRs. The vetting
agency shall raise consolidated queries, if any, which will be forwarded to the State
Government through Ministry, which will be required to furnish replies to the same
within a period of 15 days. If these queries are not settled within 15 days of
communication, the State Government will be given another 15 days for furnishing
replies to the query from the vetting agency, failing which it will presumed that the
State is not interested to pursue the project and the said project will stand rejected.
However, if the State Government finds it difficult to collect data for a reply and gives
cogent and substantial reasons, further time of up to 30 days may be provided and
not beyond.
(c) V etting agency will give techno-economic vetting of the projects within one month
from receipt of replies to the consolidated queries within a period of one month. In
case any further query is raised because of unsatisfactory replies or issues arising,
these should be settled before or on the date the project is placed for sanction before
the Screening Committee.
(d) The line Ministries/NITI Aayog/NEC will be approached in parallel for non-duplication
certificates and for certifying if the project is fit for gap funding. The line Ministries/
NITI Aayog/NEC shall give their comments/observations within one month else it will
be presumed to be clear for non-duplication and gap funding angle. In any event,

(e) NLCPR Committee meeting shall be convened periodically to consider sanctioning of
the cleared projects, duly vetted by the vetting agency.

3.9.1 The Committee considered in detail the issue of merger of NEC with the Ministry of DoNER
and shifting of its headquarters to Shillong on the anology of the Space Department and
Department of Atomic energy and designating the Secretary to the Ministry of DoNER as  ex-
officio Secretary of NEC.  The argument put forth was that Ministry of DoNER has to play
coordinating role with the State Governments and oversee/monitor the execution of projects which
can better be done from Shillong rather than Delhi.  The Committee considered the views of the
Cabinet Secretary on the role of the Ministry of DoNER as coordinating Ministry and according
to him the coordination can be best done from Delhi where other Ministries are located and shifting

DoNER has to attend meetings in the Committee of Secretaries, Cabinet meetings and it would be
difficult for the Secretary to shuffle from Shillong to Delhi. The Committee would also like to
underline the submission of the DoNER Secretary that ‘otherwise there would be better synergy’.
3.9.2 The Committee is of the strong view that if the headquarters of the Ministry of DoNER is
shifted to Shillong, it would be in a better position to monitor the effective implementation of
projects due to on-the-spot supervision. Therefore, the Committee is not in agreement with the views

monitoring would inject better synergy in the overall execution of the projects.  With the
Headquarters at Shillong, the Officers of the Ministry would be more accountable and more
focussed to their duties. Headquarters of the Ministry at Shillong would also provide opportunity

Governments and implementing agencies. The Committee, therefore, recommends that the
Government may consider shifting the headquarters of the Ministry of DoNER to Shillong and have
a camp office in Delhi to facilitate meeting with other Ministries or organizations in Delhi.
(Paras 5.23.1 and 5.23.2)

3.10 ROLES OF MINISTRY OF DONER AND NEC AND SYNERGY BETWEEN THEM
3.10.1 It was admitted before the Committee by the Secretary, DoNER that the Ministry of DoNER
