to play a proactive role in planning and implementing the Central projects/schemes/policies
implemented in the NE States. The State Governments also feel that the existence of the Ministry
of  DoNER, has, also led the line Ministries to neglect their responsibilities for the development
of the region, leaving it all to the Ministry of DoNER with its meager NLCPR resources. The
Committee also notes that the Cabinet Secretariat has denied this and stated that the percentage
utilization of 10% earmarked allocation has been increasing steadily over the past ten years.
3.10.2 The Committee, however, agrees that the Ministry of DoNER has not been able to play the
role assigned to it very effectively because of various factors discussed in the proceeding

40
paragraphs. However , the Committee is of the view that the Ministry of DoNER can play a bigger
and effective role in shaping the regional developmental priorities and implementing the regional
or State-specific programmes and projects. Active involvement of the Ministry of DoNER is a
precondition in deciding the policies, programmes, schemes, and projects by the Planning
Commission and line Ministries meant for NE region. The Committee, therefore, is of the strong
view that there is urgent need to review and redefine the role of the Ministry of DoNER in
coordinating and liaising with the line Ministries.   There should be a clear cut defined relationship
between the Planning Commission, the Ministry of DoNER, and the NEC for dovetailing and
synergizing of developmental plans, projects, and schemes and a mechanism for such coordination
should be evolved. The Committee is of the considered view that the Secretary, DoNER should be
equipped with more administrative and sanctioning powers to facilitate the smooth implementation
of developmental projects. The Committee further recommends that the Ministry of DoNER should
expand its project portfolio to include projects other than infrastructure sector, including projects
in tourism, agriculture, horticulture, animal husbandry etc., besides loan linkages for these sectors.
(Paras 5.24.1 and 5.24.2)
Action Taken
3.10.3 As recommended by the Hon’ble Committee, the Ministry has started giving focus on
projects in sectors like Organic Farming,  Animal Husbandry, Horticulture, Rural Livelihoods etc.
Further Recommendation
3.10.4 The Committee finds that the Ministry of DoNER has just indicated that the Ministry
is expanding its project-portfolios in certain fields viz. Animal Husbandary, Organic
Farming, horticulture and Rural livelihood but has not apprised the Committee of action
taken even in brief in these field and the outcome thereof.
3.10.5 The Committee further observes that the Government has not furnished its action
taken details even the views on the Committee’s recommendation on enhancing
administrative and sanctioning powers to facilitate the speedy and effective implementation
of development plan/projects/scheme/programme.  The Committee, in this regard, in
conformity to the view of Government of Sikkim as expressed in Committee’s meeting held
on 27th July, 2015 reiterates its recommendation that the Secretary, Ministry of DoNER
should have more administrative and sanctioning powers for entailing a booster dose to
development process in NER States.
3.10.6 The Committee is express its concern to observe that Government in its action taken
notes has not furnished any information on steps taken in regard to Committee’s
recommendation for strengthening the role of Ministry and measures undertaken/being
undertaken for striking operational synergy between the Ministry of DoNER and NEC.  The
Committee, therefore, reiterates its recommendation as made in Para 5.24.1 and suggests
that the Ministry of DoNER must play pro-action role.

CHAPTER-IV
RECOMMENDATION/OBSERV ATION IN RESPECT OF WHICH FINAL REPLY OF THE
GOVERNMENT HA VE NOT BEEN RECEIVED
Recommendation
4.1 PROBLEM OF INADEQUATE MANPOWER IN CEA
4.1.1 The Committee also notes that the Ministry of Power gave two reasons for the delayed
concurrence to schemes by CEA i) multi-disciplinary discussion process and ii) inadequate man
power in CEA. In view of the Committee, while due diligence and discussion can not be
compromised and Power Ministry has not much role nor should it try to curtail it, but ‘inadequate
man power’ is well within its domain, which should not have been allowed to take toll on the
clearance of the power projects. The Committee is not at all convinced with the second reason and
therefore recommends that all necessary steps be taken to address the problem of inadequate
manpower in CEA at the earliest so that power projects are cleared in an expeditious manner to
meet the country’ s growing demand of the power, particularly North East.
(Para 5.8.2)
Action Taken
4.1.2 Ministry of Power has since been asked to act on recommendation of the Parliamentary
Standing Committee and take all necessary steps to address the problem of inadequate manpower
in Central Electricity Authority at the earliest so that power projects are cleared in an expeditious
manner to meet the country’s growing demand for power particularly in North Eastern Region.

RECOMMENDA TIONS/OBSERV ATIONS — A T A GLANCE
AVOIDANCE OF PROCEDURAL DELAY
The Committee observes that in compliance with the Committee’s recommendation
for avoidance of procedural delay and direction given it its meeting held on 27 th July, 2015,
the Ministry of DoNER in tandem with the State Governments and the concerned line
Ministries has undertaken a number of measures from the stage of conceptualization of
scheme, preparation and submission of priority list, expeditious processing/execution of
projects under NLCPR scheme, setting detailed guidelines and simplification of procedures
for preparing and submission and vetting of DPRs, sanctioning, allocation and release of
funds for timely implementation and completion of projects.  The Committee, however,
would like to be apprised of perceptible outcome of the measures so undertaken on the
ground level in the form of period of time reduced in clearance of projects and its
completion in comparison to pre and post reforms phase on removal of all unnecessary
procedural delays.  The kernel spirit of the Committee’s recommendation made in para
5.2.1 of the Committee’s 173 rd Report is to give fillip to developmental process in NER
through procedural facilitation and timely implementation of policies, programmes, schemes
and projects meant for all round balanced development of the region.
(Para 1.1.8)
The Committee further recommends that the Ministry of DoNER should take up the
issue of revisiting the instant specification in guidelines for reserving 25% of new projects
for backward areas which is at present vague and therefore needs modification on the lines
of autonomous territorial /district council. (Para 1.1.9)
The Committee also recommends that the Ministry of DoNER should persuade the
line ministries to arrange training /workshops for the State Government officials and for
potential vendors nominated by States as part of the Ministry’s Vendor Development efforts.
The Committee believes that such measures would enable the State Government officials
for preparation of DPRs with great specification and on rationale basis to take into account
detailed survey and baseline facts.  The Committee further desires that the request of the
State Governments for incorporating the cost of preparation of DPRs in the project cost
should be considered at the earliest and the same may be laid down in the NLCPR
guidelines. (Para 1.1.10)
The Committee observes that no guidelines have been set up on frequency of
meeting of the NLCPR Committee and timeline for consideration  and sanctioning of
cleared projects.  Therefore, the Committee desires that the meeting of the NLCPR should
be convened periodically with a set time frame, known to the State Governments so that
42

43
requisite information may be furnished to the NLCPR Committee well in advance.  Also,
timelines for consideration and sanctioning of projects should be let up to avoid delays on
their part. (Para 1.1.11)
CAPACITY CONSTRAINTS
The Committee may be apprised of the action plan prepared with regard to capacity building
i.e. technical and execution capabilities of State Government. (Para 1.4.3)
LACUNAE ON THE PART OF THE STATE GOVERNMENTS
The Committee would like to be apprised of the recommendations of inter-ministerial
working group on development of transport network in North Eastern Region alongwith
action taken by the Government thereon.  The Committee would further desire to know
about progress on 3000 MW Debang Power Project that was to be executed by NHPC,
Arunachal Package for road construction of 740 K.M, decision granting scheme of providing
100% central assistance to NER states for taking up river development works.
(Para 1.6.7)
FINANCIAL SUPPORT TO AIRPORTS IN NE
The Committee notes the inability of DoNER/NEC to provide 100% financial support to
airports in NE.  The Ministry of Finance may look into this aspect and find a way out for
the problem. (Para 1.9.4)
GENERAL RECOMMENDATIONS
The Committee desires that Ministry of DoNER should take pro-active follow up
steps with the Ministry of Heavy Industries and also appeal to the private sector for making
investment for industries providing construction material in NER so that the problem of non
availability of construction material like cement, steel, etc is well taken up in the long
term. (Para 1.14.2)
SEPARATION OF ALLOCATIONS FOR NLCPR AND NEC SCHEMES FROM ANNUAL PLANS
OF STATES
The Committee, in its meeting held on 27
th July, 2015, came across the suggestion
of separation of allocation of NLCPR and NEC scheme from the annual plan of States.  The
Committee observes that against allocation of ````` 230 crore for the year 2014-15 under
NLCPR for the Government of Nagaland only ````` 54 crore was released thus leaving shortfall
of 76% of the sanctioned amount thereby instilling a huge deficit causing great concern and
loss for a resource constrained State i.e. Nagaland which ultimately to led to accumulation
of in completed projects and retained projects.  The Committee, therefore, recommends that
to improve the process of selection and implementation of projects, the funds available for
NLCPR and NEC may be sub allocated to NER States upfront i.e. at the beginning of the
financial year so that State Government must be aware of funding pattern well in advance.
This will allow them to make ‘Priority List’ of the projects besides ensuring enhanced active
participation of States besides retaining the power of sanctioning and supervision of projects
under the jurisdiction of the Ministry of DoNER. (Para 2.6.6)

44
FINAL APPROVED COST OF PROJECTS
The Committee reiterates its recommendation that the final approved cost of the
projects must be communicated to the State Government well in advance so that project
gets a take off without financial snags.  The Committee, therefore, strongly recommends
that the Ministry of Finance, NITI Ayog and the line Ministries should take care of
grievances of the State Government on this count and accordingly redress the grievances by
apprising the State Government of information about the whole process of finalization of
cost of the projects well in advance so that the State Government get enough time for
suitable amendment in their project plan for better execution of the project. (Para  3.1.3)
ARBITARY RETENTION AND SANCTIONING OF PROJECTS
The Committee is of the view that the contention of NER State Governments about
the sanctioning of projects with much lower cost as compared to the proposed amount in the
DPR must be examined carefully keeping in account all cost consideration and ensuring that
the final approved cost of the project should not have a bearing on quality of infrastructure
creation as that may pose a great threat/hurdle to development process in NER.
(Para  3.2.3)
POWER SECTOR
The Committee understands that there is need to give boost to the transport and
communication infrastructure, thereby requiring Comprehensive Plan for laying road
network in a time bound manner to expedite the development of the projects in far-flung
areas of NER and accordingly it has recommended for striking a coordinated and
collaborative working in this direction. The Committee recommends that operational
efficiency of implementing agencies viz. BRO is required to be enhanced.  The Committee
further recommends that undertaken course of action must entail perceptile changes on the
ground level, thereby requiring also that the Ministry of Power and the Ministry of DoNER
must work in tandem to ensure optimum utilization of power generation potential in a time
bound manner as continued supply of power is itself a basic infrastructure for other
industries and development projects. (Para  3.3.4)
AGGREGATE TECHNICAL AND COMMERCIAL (AT&C) LOSSES
The Committee notes that the progress of major physical activities under
Restructured Accelerated Power Development and Reforms Programmes (R-APDRP) by the
NER  States are at various stages of completion.  The Committee impresses that all out
efforts should be taken for expeditious completion of physical activities so that Aggregate
Technical and Commercial (AT&C) losses are minimized/eliminated in NER.  The Committee
alos recommends that the Ministry of DoNER must impress upon the State Governments of
Arunachal Pradesh and Nagaland submission of DPRs of part B projects for sanctioned to
enable the Ministry of Power to push reform programme in the direction of minimization
of distribution losses without further delay. (Para  3.5.4)
ENHANCING OPERATIONAL EFFICIENCY OF BORDER ROAD ORGANISATION
The Committee expresses its anguish to observe the evasive reply of Ministry of
DoNER.  The representatives of Government of Sikkim in Committee’s meeting held on

45
27th July, 2015 stated about operation efficiency of BRO i.e. limitation of 10 kms of road
construction by a single unit of BRO in a year which is in fact, also in the Committee’s
view point not at all impressive but rather disturbing.  The Committee, therefore, reiterates
its recommendation that the Ministry of DoNER take follow up action with MORTH
suggesting BRO for undertaking requisite steps for enhancing its operational efficiency for
meaningful completion of road project within set time frame. (Para  3.6.3)
OBSERVANCE OF NLCPR GUIDELINES
The Committee’s takes notes of merits of simplified procedure with regard to NLCPR
scheme, however, the Committee desires that line Ministry should adhere in relation to
vetting of DPRs of NLCPR projects to examine the broad outline feasibility and correctness
of DPRs, as per the guidelines for administration of NLCPR and avoid arbitrariness and
irrelevant observation for speedy clearance of projects and thereafter completion of projects
without time and cost overruns.  The Committee in its meeting held on 27
th July, 2015
during its interaction with representative of Government of Nagaland came across instances
of procedural delay due to retention of 37 projects of Government of Nagaland from
2010-11 till 2014-15 because vetting process kept on going as there was no time limit set
for vetting up DPRs. The Committee, therefore, reiterates its recommendation made in
Para 5.15.1 and recommends further that the Ministry of DoNER should examine the
possibility of outsourcing vetting of DPRs to competent public sector agencies like

College)  for speedy vetting of infrastructure projects. (Para  3.7.3)

rd
